- **Derivability** (#1325): `PrimitiveType` production added to `TypeNoNullable` and `PrimaryAtom` (with the `T?(x)` type-reading-wins note); `UnaryExpr` made right-recursive (`not not x`, `- -x`); `NullCoalesce` admits `?? throw …`; the retired pre-v0.97 `where T is owned` constraint form and `ModifierConstraint` deleted, the orphaned accessor `GenericConstraints?` removed, the SetterParamSpec comment recited to §22.3/§23.3. The enum-operator fork is **not** bundled: filed as #1381.

#### Record equality, consolidated (#1326)

§9.2 restated as **one recursive rule over storage components**; admissible component types now include `T?` (null-safe `=` per §8.4/§7.11) and non-owning inline arrays (element-wise per §8.3); the undefined "sealed reference type with content equality" clause **deleted**. §8.3's stale "Body-only record | compile error" row corrected. §9.3 gains the combined-form eligibility rule (positional fields count as storage components; disqualifiers suppress with the use-site error) and extends the use-site-error discipline to purely-positional records with non-admissible fields (closing a reference-equality footgun). §9.8 delegates to §9.2 instead of paraphrasing. **#1249-A narrowed:** an `override ToString` now suppresses only auto-`ToString`; equality survives (through v0.157 it revoked the whole package — the v0.156 reasoning never argued formatting should kill equality). §8.5 aligned.

#### Equality consistency, enforced (#1338)

- **Co-declaration rule** (§25.2): a record/enum overloading homogeneous `=`/`<>` must also declare `Equals(T)` and `override GetHashCode` — compiler-enforced, mirroring §8.3's Equals→GetHashCode rule. (IntPtr/UIntPtr intrinsics exempt.)
- **Equality-bearing** joins the §3.6 derived-property table; `Dictionary`/`OwnedDictionary` keys and `Set`/`OwnedSet` elements require it **at the instantiation site** (stdlib §4.8/§4.10), replacing the unenforceable "must provide consistent Equals and GetHashCode" prose.

#### Conversion ruling (§5.2, from #1322's merge adjudication)

Explicit `bool`→integer is **admitted** (total: `false`→`0`, `true`→`1`; the `int(r = null)` exit-code and branchless-counting idioms). `bool(n)` remains an error in both forms — partial and truthiness-shaped — as does `bool`→`float`/`double`/`decimal`/`char`. The asymmetry is deliberate and recorded in §5.2.

#### Migration

Mostly source-compatible. Tightenings: the §25.2 co-declaration rule (a record overloading `=` without `Equals`/`GetHashCode` now errors — the fix is stating them); hash-container instantiation over non-equality-bearing record keys/elements now errors at the instantiation. Loosenings: `int(b)` compiles; records with `override ToString` regain auto-equality; negative constant patterns and `T?`/inline-array record components become expressible/eligible. Compiler alignment for the new checks and eligibility extensions follows in-run; the parser already implements the #1320/#1321 rules.

<a id="sec-v0-158-to-v0-159-changelog"></a>
### v0.159 changelog (v0.158 → v0.159)

v0.159 is the **conversions-and-typing revision**: four families of rules the compiler already implemented but the spec never stated are now normative. Nearly docs-only (probe-level verification in-run). (Issues: #1323, #1324, #1337, #1340; also settles #184's documented-vs-rejected fork.)

- **Constant narrowing** (§5.1, #1323): a compile-time integer constant implicitly converts to any integer type containing its value; out-of-range constants error (never truncate). Cross-referenced from §15.4/§10.2/§18.1.
- **MinValue literals** (§4.2): the 2³¹/2⁶³ magnitudes admitted solely as immediate operands of unary `-` — `int.MinValue`/`long.MinValue` become writable.
- **Typed-context widening** (§4.2/§18.1, the #184 fork settled): an oversized unsuffixed decimal literal is admitted at an explicitly-declared integer target it fits; untyped contexts still error toward a suffix. Rationale: the width is taken only from a written target and range-checked — the suffix discipline's purpose survives; rejecting would break the corpus for no safety gain.
- **Common-type (join) rule** (§20/§19.1/§21.9, #1324): A-into-B-or-B-into-A only (widening, T→T?, subtype→base); no sibling LUB (deliberately unlike §31.2.1 catch bindings); throw arms bottom-typed; condition-first evaluation and selected-arm-only evaluation stated; case/when expression type = left-fold of arm types; §21.9's discard rules applied per arm in statement position (resolving its tension with §19.1).
- **`?` idempotent under substitution** (§7.10 + C.4 + stdlib §5 note, #1337): `T?` at T=`U?` is `U?`; no two-level optional; the `*OrNull`-at-nullable-T ambiguity documented with the recommended shapes; bare-T storage follows §7.9.
- **Range `Contains` vs direction** (§16.3/§16.4/§16.6, #1340): normative extent formula (min/max endpoints, exclusivity, null-open sides, Step-independent) — `50 in 100..0` is true; `IsEmpty` reworded to iteration; **range patterns read bounds directionally as written** (reversed patterns match nothing) with the deliberate pattern-vs-Contains asymmetry recorded; the circular §17.5 reference in the surrogate paragraph fixed.

#### Migration
None expected: every rule codifies implemented behavior. (In-run probes verify: reversed-range pattern non-match, MinValue literal forms, `T?`-idempotence corners; divergences found become implementation fixes, not spec changes.)

<a id="sec-v0-159-to-v0-160-changelog"></a>
### v0.160 changelog (v0.159 → v0.160)

v0.160 is the **members revision**: the call/parameter-modifier composition matrix gets defined, extensions and operators get their resolution cores, the arrow-body family gets its one missing form, and two small syntax seams close. (Issues: #1335, #1343-remainder, #1344, #1345, #1346, #1347.)

- **out-var annotations** (#1335): §22.6's stray annotated forms struck — the inline `out var x` never takes a type annotation (§22.4 was always explicit); typed disambiguation = pre-declared local.
- **Modifier composition** (#1344): A.4 Argument gains `out owned var` (the thrice-stated prose form is now derivable) and restricts named arguments to plain values (`M(out var x := n)` has no reading); `out _` defined against both out kinds (owned discard = unbound owned temporary, end-of-statement disposal; both-overloads-present ⇒ ambiguity error); defaults permitted only on unmodified/`owned` parameters, with the trailing-defaults rule stated; primary constructors take plain/`owned` parameters only.
- **Arrow bodies** (#1345): a unit-returning method takes the assignment arrow the accessors always had (`method SetX(v: int) => _x := v;`); the remaining per-context divergences recorded with reasons in rationale §3.5 (lambda `;`-collision, operators value-only, methods already have the bare block).
- **Extensions** (#1346): the implicit type-parameter binding rule stated (bare single-segment identifier in argument position of the extended type binds fresh, always, with a shadowing warning — the only implicit type-parameter binding in the language; "resolution-wins" declined as action-at-a-distance); extension members are `public`/`internal` only; extension properties expression-bodied only.
- **Operators** (#1347): declaring-type-operand requirement; the two-operand-types union resolution rule with no auto-commutation and the both-types ambiguity error; `public` made normative (A.4 narrowed); C.10 bullets added.
- **Syntax seams closed** (#1343 remainder): type aliases bind with `:=` (was `=`, the sole exception — "all bindings introduce with `:=`" is now exceptionless; 9 examples migrated); `destructor` parens-less form recorded as intentional (rationale §3.6).

#### Migration
Tightenings: named ref/out/owned arguments (were undefined-but-parseable) now rejected; non-public operators rejected; protected/private extension members rejected; block-bodied extension properties rejected; defaults on ref/out rejected. Type alias `=` → `:=` is source-breaking but trivially mechanical. Compiler alignment for all of v0.160 rides the wave-3 lanes (the `out owned var` parse is #1305's fix; the owned-`out _` disposal semantics subsumes the #1315 scratch-slot family for owned outs).

<a id="sec-v0-160-to-v0-161-changelog"></a>
### v0.161 changelog (v0.160 → v0.161)

v0.161 is the **ownership-honesty revision**: the one remaining zero-disposal path closes, the soundness claims are rescoped to exactly what is checked, and the owning-enumeration protocol loses its anomalous destructive getter. (Issues: #1328, #1331, #1349, #1360.)

- **Drop-on-overwrite** (§28.7 rewritten, #1328): assignment to an owned field or plain-`var` owned local now disposes the displaced live value (RHS-first; null/moved-from displaced values dispose nothing; explicit prior `Dispose()` stays legal via idempotence, so all correct v0.160 code is behavior-preserved). The "compiler warning on undisposed overwrite" subsection is deleted; the disposers-don't-throw discussion is rewritten for the new ordering (the manual pattern's exception-unsafe window no longer exists on the implicit path). New Appendix C.3 invariant. §28.8's commentary updated. The §28.3 exactly-once claim becomes true without carve-outs. Move-only inline-array whole-value reassignment retains §15.3's manual discipline (deferred with its own issue — #747 interaction). *Compiler: locals half already shipped (#913/#1054); the fields half is a wave-4 ownership lane; spec-ahead-of-implementation until it lands.*
- **Borrow honesty** (§28.3, #1331): the producers-table borrow row and the factory-methods text are restated structurally (instance ⇒ receiver-sourced borrow; static ⇒ owned-with-warning; documentation phrases carry no classification weight — `owned` is the only transfer signal); the borrow-into-field bullet separates the decidable assignment-site check from the trusted caller-side lifetime obligation, naming the checked-mode `DisposedAccessException` backstop and the unchecked-mode UB honestly; the closing soundness sentence is rescoped to what is actually guaranteed.
- **`TakeCurrent()`** (§29.1/§29.2/§30.7 + stdlib §4.13, #1349): the owning enumerators' destructive `Current: owned T` property is replaced by an ordinary owned-returning method — the language's only destructive property getter is removed (it violated §28.6 as written; §23 itself prescribes a method for transfer-out). Protocol misuse (read/take before first advance, after exhaustion, double-take) is a **defined `InvalidOperationException`** (was undefined behavior), normative for stdlib/compiler-generated enumerators, contractual for user ones. *Compiler: builtin-member rename + desugaring + IOE guards ride wave-4.*
- **`using var` as readonly-local** (rationale §17.8, #1360): the no-op-disposal admission documented honestly (tolerated for uniformity, not the endorsed idiom; runtime-`const` stays on the deferred list). No diagnostic added — §28.10 sanctions scope-pinning.

#### Migration
Drop-on-overwrite is behavior-preserving for all correct code and un-leaks previously-leaking code. `TakeCurrent()` is a mechanical rename for owning-enumerator users (the for-desugarings are compiler-internal). No other changes.

<a id="sec-v0-161-to-v0-162-changelog"></a>
### v0.162 changelog (v0.161 → v0.162)

v0.162 is the **async-and-exceptions revision**, executing the #1362 deadlock proposal and closing the async/exception findings of the 2026-07 review; it also carries the owner-prompted range-membership correction. (Issues: #1362, #1332, #1333, #1340-revision, #1350, #1352, #1379; RFC #811 resolved by ruling.)

- **Blocking waits are contextual** (§30.3/§22.13, #1362): `Wait()`/`Result` on an incomplete task are legal only outside domains (startup code on the main thread — the same mechanism that drives async `Main`); inside a domain continuation they are a deterministic deadlock and become a compile error in `async` bodies plus a runtime `InvalidOperationException` elsewhere. §22.13's previously-prescribed (and deadlocking) `Wait()` static-init pattern is replaced by eager-init-in-async-`Main` and the lazy-task-accessor patterns. New C.6 posture throughout.
- **Pattern A slots are owned or chained** (§30.5, #1332): a `return await <source>` transfers the *source task* into the outer task (destructor disposes the chain link, never the borrowed result) — "disposing the task disposes the result" holds transitively. **`Task.WhenAny` returns `Task<int>`** (the winner's index): the former `Task<Task>` was unconstructible under this section's own rules. Rationale §12.2 Step 4 rewritten (the "task borrows from the repository" story was unimplementable).
- **OwnedTask spends on all edges** (§30.4/§30.5/C.6, #1352): the first await consumes the operand regardless of outcome (fault/cancel included; retry = bind a fresh task); C.6 now distinguishes owned operands (second await = compile-time moved-from read) from borrowed ones (runtime IOE).
- **`OwnedTask<T>.Result` blessed** (§30.3, #1379): a completed-task read in an owned-consuming position transfers ownership exactly like `await` (the implementation's #1250 semantics, now normative); subject to the same blocking-context rules.
- **TCS closure-capture exception defined** (§30.11, #1333): four compiler-checkable conditions replace "recognized by shape"; the registration callback must be one-shot; repeating registrations are outside the exception (the old keyboard-event example — itself a use-after-dispose under the structural proof — replaced by a one-shot block-device read).
- **Exception model completed** (§31/§22.7/stdlib, #1350 + RFC #811): the base `Exception` surface is declared for the first time (ctors, `Message`, `StackTrace: string`, `CauseChain`); **cause chaining is by snapshot** — the `(message, cause)` constructor borrows the cause and copies `ExceptionInfo` records (type/message/stack) into the new exception's flattened `CauseChain`, never retaining the instance — resolving #811 inside the caught-exception-is-a-borrow model with zero new ownership rules (a live `InnerException` on user exceptions is deliberately declined; `TypeInitializationException`'s stays the one runtime-owned live reference, now stated to be process-lifetime-owned and exempt from dispose-after-arm). The throw-in-finally supersede rule is stated in §31.2 itself (superseded exception disposed exactly once — same for guard supersede); wrapping constructors take the caught exception as a borrow and snapshot it; `ArgumentException`'s surface declared; `StackTrace` is a `string` (guides fixed).
- **Range membership corrected** (§16.3/§16.6 + stdlib §9.8, revising v0.159 after owner review of #1340): `Contains(v)` = *nonempty under iteration* ∧ within-extent — an empty range contains nothing (`50 in 100..0` is now `false`, matching Rust/Python); `IsEmpty` and `Contains` agree; range patterns and `in` agree exactly on stepless forms (the v0.159 asymmetry is deleted); constant reversed range patterns get a mandatory never-matches warning; stepped descending ranges keep their members.

#### Migration
Tightenings: in-domain `Wait()`/`Result` (was a deadlock at runtime — now diagnosed); `50 in 100..0`-style extent membership over iteration-empty ranges (write `Math.Min/Max` comparisons for unordered intervals). `WhenAny` consumers switch from the (unconstructible) winner task to its index. Everything else is definition of previously-undefined or unstated behavior. Compiler alignment rides wave-4: the Wait/Result sema-reject + runtime guard (unblocked by #1377's RaiseAsync re-lower), WhenAny index, spend-on-fault, Contains flip + warning, Exception surface/CauseChain, TakeCurrent (v0.161), fields drop-on-overwrite (v0.161).

<a id="sec-v0-162-to-v0-163-changelog"></a>
### v0.163 changelog (v0.162 → v0.163)

v0.163 is the **domains-and-system revision**: the statics side door closes, termination gets defined, FFI callbacks are inverted to the forms that actually lower, the sendability coordination text is reconciled, and event-raise reentrancy is pinned. (Issues: #1363, #1364, #1366, #1367, #1369. The module-system chapter, #1365, is deliberately its own following revision.)

- **Statics and domains** (§22.12 + §30.14, #1363): statics are process-global; lazy initialization is runtime-synchronized once-semantics; a *mutable* static of non-synchronized type is a compile error; readonly immutable content is unrestricted; class-typed readonly singletons carry a declaration warning naming the cross-domain obligation; static events' subscriber lists are runtime-synchronized. §30.14's headline invariant now cites the statics rules instead of silently excluding them.
- **Sendability list reconciled** (§30.14, #1364): `Shared<T>`'s v0.140 conditional rule replaces the stale blanket exclusion; `Mutex`/`Semaphore`/atomics stated sendable (their purpose), `Lock` guards domain-bound.
- **Termination defined** (§33.3, #1366): uncaught exception ⇒ exit 70 + typed/chained report to stderr, shutdown sequence still runs; live spawned domains at `Main`'s completion are **abandoned** (join explicitly if their work matters); `Environment.Exit` initiates the same shutdown from any domain and never returns.
- **FFI callbacks inverted** (§32.8/§32.10, #1367): static methods and *non-capturing lambdas* are admitted (both are bare fn pointers); bound instance references and capturing lambdas are rejected (they need an environment the FFI does not define) — the previous rule admitted exactly the wrong set. Environmentless callbacks may be retained by native code past the call (process-lifetime code addresses; foreign-thread discipline per §30.12/§30.14 governs what they may touch). The `errno()` example corrected.
- **Event raise takes a snapshot** (§24.5, #1369): in-flight raises are unaffected by subscribes/unsubscribes from handlers; self-unsubscribing one-shot listeners are thereby well-defined.
- **Diagnostic identity is implementation-defined** (Appendix D, #1369): conformance classifies accept/warn/reject; no error-code registry until multiple implementations exist.

#### Migration
Tightenings: mutable non-synchronized statics become errors (the sanctioned shapes: synchronized types, readonly immutables, or domain-confined design); capturing/bound FFI callbacks become errors (pass state through the C user-data pointer). `WhenAny`-era note: none. Compiler alignment rides waves 4–5 (statics checks, static-event sync, snapshot raise, FFI admission flip, exit-code path).

<a id="sec-v0-163-to-v0-164-changelog"></a>
### v0.164 changelog (v0.163 → v0.164)

v0.164 is the **module-system revision** — §2 grows from ~70 lines to a real chapter, closing the review's one chapter-sized hole (#1365).

- **Circular imports compile as one unit** (§2.5): import cycles form strongly-connected components; an SCC is the compilation unit (sources compiled together, one artifact per member still emitted; partial-SCC builds are errors naming the missing members); between SCCs resolution stays artifact-based in condensed topological order. This replaces the jointly-impossible pair "resolution reads compiled artifacts" + "circular type-level imports are permitted".
- **Import aliases** (§2.2 + A.1): `import M.N as X;` — a file-scoped qualifier; bare names and the full module name stay usable.
- **Collision rule** (§2.2): same public name from two imports ⇒ the bare name is ambiguous (error citing both; qualify or alias); imports never shadow one another; current-module declarations shadow imports for bare-name purposes.
- **Dotted-name resolution** (new §2.7): leftmost-first, type-wins, no backtracking; longest-module-prefix fallback; shadowing warning when a type and module prefix compete; adding an import can un-error a chain but never silently re-mean one.

#### Migration
Additive except the collision rule, which turns silent first-import-wins behavior (where an implementation had any) into an explicit ambiguity error. Compiler alignment (alias parse, ambiguity diagnostic, §2.7 order, SCC build mode) is a wave-5 lane with probe-first discipline — the implementation's current behavior for each corner is measured before changing it.

<a id="sec-v0-164-to-v0-165-changelog"></a>
### v0.165 changelog (v0.164 → v0.165)

v0.165 is the **standard-library rules revision** — the review's stdlib findings land as one batch. (Issues: #1327, #1342, #1353, #1354, #1355, #1356, #1357, #1358, #1359, #1375.)

- **Owning-collection elements are class/interface only** (#1327): the three-way contradiction resolved in the v0.102-recorded direction; stdlib §4.2 rewritten, spec §14.4's "proper class types" phrase corrected; value-typed elements rejected at instantiation.
- **Stream read contract** (#1375): `Array<T>` gains the sized constructor `(size, fill)`; the windowed Read/Write forms range over `Count` (never grow); span-taking Read/Write/Async overloads added (#1355) as the preferred forms — the canonical read loop is finally writable.
- **Byte-worlds bridges** (#1358): deserializers accept `ReadOnlyArraySpan<byte>`; the endianness accessors are mirrored onto the Array-span family; `File.WriteAllBytes` takes `ReadOnlySpan<byte>` — file→parse and serialize→file are zero-copy.
- **Inline arrays join the ecosystem** (#1342): intrinsic `ToArray(): owned Array<T>` and `Contains` (making `x in arr` work through §17.5) — §15.1.2/§17.5 rewritten.
- **Lazy-query consumption points** (#1353): the normative three-point list (enumerate/terminal, compose, pass-as-IEnumerable) with the untracked-callee honesty note; no Query<T> head type (declined — it would break the §5 surface and re-erase at the upcast).
- **Collection-family consistency** (#1354): SortedDictionary/SortedSet gain their IReadOnlyCollection conformance (making documented iteration legal); SortedDictionary.TryGetValue takes `out V`; SortedSet gets Add/TryAdd per the §4.10 convention; Dictionary Keys/Values become read-only views; borrowing Stack/Queue retype to IReadOnlyCollection with explicit Contains. The hash-vs-sorted comparer split and the literal duplicate policies are kept and recorded (rationale).
- **Directory/Path/Convert normativity** (#1356): full surfaces enumerated; the Convert elisions expanded; Convert ruled a kept familiarity alias (rationale §15.x) with no cross-primitive role.
- **Temporal ordering and construction** (#1357): DateTime/TimeSpan/DateOnly/TimeOnly/Guid gain IComparable/IEquatable with stated CompareTo semantics (ticks; Guid = canonical-byte lexicographic — the .NET trap called out), component constructors, Ticks/FromTicks, Unix conversions, Guid.FromByteArray, and full DateOnly/TimeOnly declarations.
- **Naming conventions recorded** (#1359): acronym/width rules stated (IEEERemainder and IeeeEquals both correct under one rule); Random.NextLong → **NextInt64**; the enumeration-interface I-prefix resolves in #1372's rename train.

#### Migration
Tightenings: value-element owning collections (`OwnedArray<int>`) become instantiation errors — use `Array<T>`/`OwnedBuffer<T>`; SortedSet.Add's bool form becomes TryAdd. Everything else is additive or a documented alias. Compiler alignment is the wave-5 stdlib lane (instantiation check + ~8 test migrations, intrinsics, retypes, new members).

<a id="sec-v0-156-to-v0-157-changelog"></a>
### v0.157 changelog (v0.156 → v0.157)

v0.157 is the **documentation-currency revision**: it brings every body section of the five documents up to date with decisions already landed (chiefly the v0.97 `Owned*` naming and the v0.150–v0.152 affine model), corrects the mechanical defects catalogued by the 2026-07 documentation review, and records previously-unrecorded syntax decisions. It changes no language capability. (Issues: #1317, #1318, #1319, #1329, #1330, #1361, #1373, plus the recording halves of #1343.)

#### Currency sweep (stale-premise text updated in place)

- **Rationale §12.1–§12.2** respelled from the retired `Task<owned T>` to `OwnedTask<T>` with a spelling note; §12.2 retitled (#1317). Historical/changelog mentions untouched.
- **Affine-model echoes swept** (#1329): spec §29.2 (iteration-variable discharge — twice), §30.1, §30.5, Appendix C.3, and stdlib §4.5/§4.13 no longer state the pre-v0.150 "compile error" rule; all now delegate to §28.3's auto-drop-with-must-use-warning. *Compiler note:* the implementation still hard-errors on an undischarged owned **iteration variable** (the §28.3 auto-drop machinery requires a plain local); this revision is spec-ahead-of-implementation on that path, as v0.151 was for Part C — the compiler follow-up is tracked in #1329.
- **Guide 1** (#1330): §5's factory guidance rewritten — the old text taught `using var fresh; … return fresh;`, which the spec rejects ("cannot move out of `using var`"), and pre-affine leak-error framing; it now teaches plain-`var` factories (exception-safe via the §28.3 exception-path discharge) and `using var` as scope-pinned. §7's closing rewritten for auto-drop. §6's dangling "Guide 4" reference now cites spec §28.8.1/§28.11 (#1319).
- **Field-narrowing justification re-led** (rationale §6.1, spec §7, Guide 2 §1): the "another thread" rationale is incoherent under the serial-domain model (v0.131); the operative reasons are unseen writers — method calls, aliases, closures, re-entrancy, and continuation interleaving at `await` — with FFI threads as the residual concurrent case.
- **Rationale §5.1** gains a supersession note (data races closed by the domain model §12.5/§12.6; the discharge error superseded by the affine model).
- **Both guides re-pinned** to the current revision (#1318), with the standing rule below.

#### New rationale body sections

- **§3.3 The value-position conditional is value-first** — records the owner ruling on #1373: the Python-style `a if c else b` is kept deliberately; the prefix `if c then a else b end` expression form and C's `?:` are recorded as considered-and-declined; the statement/expression word-order asymmetry is the accepted cost.
- **§3.4 Compound assignment is spelled `+=`, not `+:=`** — records the deliberate C-family seam in the Pascal-family operator set (#1343 recording half), with `+:=` and no-compound-assignment as considered-and-declined.
- **§5.23 The affine model** — hoists the v0.150–v0.152 why-affine reasoning from this changelog (which is "not part of the language definition") into the rationale body (#1330).

#### Mechanical defect sweep (#1361)

Spec §22.5 (example parameter renamed `when`→`at` — `when` is unconditionally reserved; the `b: int = a + 1` default respelled `:=`, re-applying the v0.79 fix); §22.6 (ConnectionPool sketch marked bodies-elided); §29.8 (illustrative-API disclaimers on both StreamReader examples); §B.2 (`step` reserved-context row corrected); Appendix C.3 (owned fields are class- **or interface**-typed, per §28.5); §13.6 (accessor visibility: **equal** visibility is permitted — aligned to the implemented rule; only *less restrictive* is an error); §13.3 + C.2 (the `polymorphic` registry recorded as the third no-visibility member); §30.7 (interface sketch gains the decided `token := CancellationToken.None` default, matching stdlib §4.12); §19.3 (a type-pattern binding is in scope in the arm's **guard** and body, as §19.4's own example requires); §17.13 (corollary recorded: a `var _` binding can never be re-assigned); A.4 (IndexerDecl's over-admitted `"static"` annotated as semantically rejected per §23.5). Stdlib §6.1 (the self-contradictory TimeoutException availability sentence); §2.4 (`GetEnvironmentVariables(): owned Dictionary<string, string>` per the §1 fresh-instance convention — compiler alignment tracked with #1361).

#### Standing rule adopted (docs workflow)

A revision that changes a premise must touch every body section that stated that premise (grep for the old vocabulary as part of mechanical validation), and the guides are re-validated and re-pinned at each revision that touches material they teach.

#### Migration

None. No capability, grammar, or behavior change; the §13.6 wording aligns the spec to the already-implemented rule.

<a id="sec-v0-165-to-v0-166-changelog"></a>
### v0.166 changelog (v0.165 → v0.166)

v0.166 is the **case-of revision** — the first of the review's breaking-syntax adoptions (#1370; RFC filed from the 2026-07 syntax pass).

- **`case Expression of Arms end`** (§19.1, Appendix A.7): the keyword `of` delimits the scrutinee from the first arm. The scrutinee becomes a **full Expression**; the multiplicative-level restriction and its mandatory-parenthesization rule (normative since v0.158, the subject of #1320/#1233) are **removed** — they existed only to substitute for the missing boundary. New rationale [§3.7](Bezel_Design_Rationale.md#sec-case-scrutinee-of-delimiter) records the trade and the declined alternatives. `when` is unaffected.
- **Diagnostic**: a missing `of` is a syntax error at the first arm token, worded "expected `of` after the case scrutinee".

#### Migration

Breaking but purely mechanical: insert `of` after every `case` scrutinee. Previously-mandatory parens around additive/bitwise/range scrutinies may be dropped (they remain legal). The conformance corpus and the project's own test/example sources are migrated with this revision's compiler train.

<a id="sec-v0-166-to-v0-167-changelog"></a>
### v0.167 changelog (v0.166 → v0.167)

v0.167 is the **pattern-alternatives revision** — the second breaking-syntax adoption from the review (#1371).

- **Alternatives are `|`-separated** (§19.3, A.7 `AltPattern`, A.6 `CatchPattern`, §31.2): `1 | 2 => "low"`; `catch FormatException | OverflowException => …`. The comma is exclusively the arm/slot separator; the `=>` disambiguation lookahead is removed from the grammar.
- **Per-slot alternatives** (§19.3, A.7 `PositionalPattern`): `TwoColor(Color.Red | Color.Blue, var x)` — previously inexpressible (#1300 had banned slot alternatives to keep the comma unambiguous).
- **Members stay constants-only in case patterns**; catch alternatives stay types-only; the binding rule for `catch var e: T1 | T2` (nearest common base) is unchanged. New rationale [§3.8](Bezel_Design_Rationale.md#sec-pattern-alternatives-pipe) records the trade.
- **No bitwise-or collision** (normative note, §19.3): pattern-embedded expressions parse below `|`; the scrutinee is `of`-delimited (v0.166).

#### Migration

Breaking but purely mechanical: `,` → `|` inside pattern-alternative lists (case constant alternatives and catch multi-type lists — both syntactically identifiable). Slot separators and arm separators are untouched. The conformance corpus and the project's test/example sources are migrated with this revision's compiler train.

<a id="sec-v0-167-to-v0-168-changelog"></a>
### v0.168 changelog (v0.167 → v0.168)

v0.168 is the **owning-rename revision** — the third breaking-syntax adoption from the review (#1372, folding in #1359's I-prefix deferral).

- **`Owned…` → `Owning…`** across the owning family: `OwningArray/Dictionary/Set/Stack/Queue/LinkedList/Buffer`, `OwningTask`, `OwningTaskCompletionSource`. The two ownership axes get lexically distinct words: `owned` (container qualifier) vs `Owning` (element prefix). New rationale [§3.9](Bezel_Design_Rationale.md#sec-owning-prefix).
- **Owning interfaces gain the `I` prefix**: `IOwningEnumerable`, `IOwningEnumerator`, `IOwningAsyncEnumerable`, `IOwningAsyncEnumerator`, `IOwningList`, `IOwningCollection`; `GetOwnedEnumerator()` → `GetOwningEnumerator()` (and the async form).
- **Not renamed**: `owned` (the qualifier), `AppendOwned`/`FromOwnedResult` (they name an owned *argument*), the inline-array slot marker (deferred, §3.9), and historical changelog entries (which record the names as of their revision).

#### Migration

Breaking but purely textual: a global, word-boundary rename over the map above (no semantics change; the two-axis model of §5.11 stands unmodified). The conformance corpus, compiler type registry, diagnostics, and the project's test/example sources are migrated with this revision's compiler train; the compiler emits a renamed-type hint when an old name fails to resolve.

<a id="sec-v0-168-to-v0-169-changelog"></a>
### v0.169 changelog (v0.168 → v0.169)

v0.169 is the **call-site transfer-marker revision** — the fourth breaking-syntax adoption from the review (#1348).

- **`M(owned x)`** (§22.3, §28.3, §28.8, A.7): passing a **named owned binding** to an `owned` parameter requires the `owned` call-site marker; fresh producers stay unmarked. The previously-orphaned A.7 bare-`owned` `ArgModifiers` alternative is defined (it had no prose semantics — itself a latent grammar/prose inconsistency). Diagnostics name the fix in both directions (missing marker on a named binding; spurious marker on a borrow/fresh producer/non-owned position). New rationale [§3.10](Bezel_Design_Rationale.md#sec-call-site-transfer-marker).
- **§22.6 overload ban stands** (recorded follow-on): the marker satisfies the ban's carve-out criterion for named bindings, but lifting the ban is deliberately not part of this revision.

#### Migration

Breaking, compiler-guided: every call passing a named owned binding to an `owned` parameter gains `owned` at the argument (the missing-marker diagnostic points at each site). Fresh-producer arguments are untouched. The conformance corpus and the project's test/example sources are migrated with this revision's compiler train.

<a id="sec-v0-169-to-v0-170-changelog"></a>
### v0.170 changelog (v0.169 → v0.170)

v0.170 is the **uniform-closer revision** — the fifth and final syntax adoption from the review (#1374). Fully additive.

- **One end-label rule** (§1.6, Appendix A): `end` may optionally repeat the construct's name or introducing keyword, checked when present. Newly legal-and-checked: `end if;`, `end while;`, `end for;`, `end do;`, `end try;`, `end case;`, `end when;`, `end extension;`, `end extern;`. Bare `end;` remains valid everywhere. New rationale [§3.11](Bezel_Design_Rationale.md#sec-uniform-end-closer).

#### Migration

None — the change is additive; the entire existing corpus already conforms.

<a id="sec-v0-170-to-v0-171-changelog"></a>
### v0.171 changelog (v0.170 → v0.171)

v0.171 is the **Try-convention revision** (#1336) — the review's P6 sweep.

- **One Try shape for extraction** (stdlib §1 Conventions, §4.5/§4.7/§4.8/§4.9/§4.11, §4.17): every extraction Try's out parameter is **nullable** — `TryPop(out owned item: T?)`, `TryGetValue(key, out value: V?)`, `TryPeek(out item: T?)` — because §22.3 requires every out assigned on every exit path and the false path has only `null` to assign. This removes the third, unimplementable shape (`out owned item: T` on `where T: class` collections, reintroduced without a decision by the v0.96 rewrite against the rationale's own v0.89 rule). The nullable-return shape (`TryAcquire(): owned Lock?`, v0.77) remains the sanctioned alternative when null alone is the signal; §1 now names both shapes and when each applies.
- **Borrowing forms included** (resolving v0.77's deferred question): `Dictionary.TryGetValue`, `Stack/Queue` `TryPop`/`TryDequeue`/`TryPeek` take `out ... T?`/`V?` uniformly — value-typed instantiations read a `T?` at the call site. Uniformity was chosen over per-category shapes: one rule, honest types, and the two-overload borrow/take pattern of §22.6 keeps working.
- The `!` after a successful Try remains required — the §22.6-named flow-narrowing deferral is unchanged (copied here per the #1336 recommendation: a future revision adding flow-sensitive out-narrowing removes the `!`; the signature sweep deliberately does not wait for it).

#### Migration

Breaking for callers that declared the out recipient non-nullable: the recipient becomes `T?` (inline `out var x` forms simply infer the nullable type; explicit `var x: T := ...; Try(out x)` forms change the local's type or switch to inline-out). The compiler train migrates the corpus; call sites already using `out using var`/`out owned var` + `!` (the Guide 2 idiom) are unaffected.

<a id="sec-v0-171-to-v0-172-changelog"></a>
### v0.172 changelog (v0.171 → v0.172)

v0.172 is the **formatting revision** — discharging RFC #812's standout item together with #1339's lexical gaps and the gap review's formatting cluster.

- **`IFormattable`** (new stdlib §2.18; spec §18.5 dispatch rule): a format spec dispatches to `ToString(format)`; primitives/temporals are intrinsically formattable; user types opt in nominally; a spec on a non-formattable operand is a compile error. This closes §18.5's "passed to the value's formatter" dangling reference — there was previously nothing for a user type's spec to route to (#812 item 1).
- **The specifier vocabulary is normative and invariant-culture-only** (stdlib §2.18): integer D/X/B, floating F/E/G/P/R, temporal pattern letters, Guid D/N; unrecognized → `FormatException`. **Round-trip guarantee**: `double`/`float` no-format `ToString()` ≡ `R` ≡ shortest string that reparses identically. `C` (currency) deliberately absent — currency is culture by definition.
- **Literal braces** (spec §18.5/§18.8/A.1, #1339): `{{`/`}}` doubling in `$"…"` and `$@"…"` — a literal brace was previously unwritable in interpolated strings.
- **Hole delimitation made normative** (spec §18.5, #1339): `,`/`:` recognized only at the hole's top nesting level (brackets nest, nested literals skip); the format spec runs to the closing `}` and is brace-free. `\x` greediness stays as already specified in §18.8 (documented with workaround; not a gap).

#### Migration

Additive except: a format spec on a non-formattable operand — previously silently accepted and ignored or misrouted — is now a compile error; `{{`/`}}` in existing interpolated strings (none in the corpus — the sequence was previously meaningless) would change meaning.

<a id="sec-v0-172-to-v0-173-changelog"></a>
### v0.173 changelog (v0.172 → v0.173)

v0.173 is the **cancellation-composition revision** — adopting RFC #810's first half and recording the second half as already-existing.

- **Linked token sources** (stdlib §6.1, spec §30.8): `CreateLinked(a, b)` + `CreateLinkedAll(parents: Array<CancellationToken>)` — cancelled when any parent cancels or by the source's own `Cancel`/`CancelAfter`; already-cancelled parents cancel the child synchronously at creation (the `Register` race-free policy); disposal unregisters from parents before signalling. Intra-domain only; the parent sources must outlive the linked source (the existing source-outlives-token posture). Array form instead of variadics (§22.14's variadic decline stands).
- **`CancellationScope` declined-with-reasons**: the RFC's scope sketch duplicates existing semantics — the source destructor already cancels on dispose, so `using var cts := CancellationTokenSource.WithCancelAfter(delay);` *is* timeout-as-a-scope and every `using var` source is cancel-on-scope-exit. A wrapper type would add a name, not a capability; the idiom is now documented in §6.1 where the RFC's readers will look.
- Sequencing note: #808 (task nursery) consumes these primitives (cancel-siblings-on-fault is a linked source per child); #809 (bounded channels) is independent.

#### Migration

None — purely additive.

<a id="sec-v0-173-to-v0-174-changelog"></a>
### v0.174 changelog (v0.173 → v0.174)

v0.174 is the **back-pressure revision** — adopting RFC #809's bounded half.

- **Bounded channels** (spec §30.15, stdlib §6.9): `new Channel<T>(capacity)`; `SendAsync(owned item): Task` awaits capacity (immediate on unbounded); sync `Send` keeps never-blocks on every channel and raises the new `ChannelFullException` on a full bounded one — a producer that wants to wait says so with `await`, per the §30.3 no-blocking discipline. Close-while-waiting disposes the pending item (the buffered-items rule) and faults the send task with `ChannelClosedException`.
- **Deferred with reasons**: capacity-zero rendezvous (scheduling coupling; addable as `capacity: 0` later), `TrySend` and send-cancellation (both need a hand-the-owned-item-BACK protocol — a real ownership design, not sugar; cancellation additionally rides #1413's foundations), multi-consumer receiver cloning (RFC #809's other half — `Shared<T>` unblocked the mechanism but §28.13's domain-locality questions remain, and N single-consumer channels compose worker pools today; revisit with pipeline evidence).

#### Migration

None — purely additive.

<a id="sec-v0-174-to-v0-175-changelog"></a>
### v0.175 changelog (v0.174 → v0.175)

v0.175 is the **structured-concurrency revision** — adopting RFC #808 on the researched general capture mechanism (owner-ruled 2026-07-03: no further per-API carve-outs; full comparison in docs/proposals/capture-mechanism-808.md).

- **`scoped` parameters + storage-bounded capture** (new spec §28.14; §28.3/§28.2/§27.2/§22.3/§32/A.4/A.6 amendments): a function-typed parameter marked `scoped` lets the callee store the callback bounded by a **bounding object** (constructed / owned-return-into-`using var` / receiver) whose lifetime the caller's checker proves ends before every captured source's scope. Callee storage obligations compiler-verified (v1: direct `scoped` fields of the bounding object only — the owned-field-extraction hole both candidate designs shared is closed by construction); quiescence is the author's obligation in the §28.3 borrowed-field trust shape, backstopped by `DisposedAccessException` in checked mode; `scoped` illegal on extern. **§30.11's TCS exception re-derives as an instance** (legacy text retained until stdlib migration — no new hard-coded patterns, ever). §24 events unify as-is: `Subscribe(scoped handler)` is the owned-return form.
- **`TaskScope`** (stdlib §6.10): the nursery — `await using` only; mandatory `await Join()` as the sole re-raise site (first-fault-wins + cancel-siblings via the scope's token, the §13.5 no-aggregation posture); `DisposeAsync` drains-and-swallows; `Spawn` after close is `InvalidOperationException`; unbounded close-edge drain per the approved §28.12 note, bounded by `CancelAfter`. Intra-domain; consumes #810's primitives.
- Declined/deferred in this revision: typed-result `Spawn<T>` handles (results flow via captured sinks), block-form sugar, cross-domain nurseries (§30.14 capture-free entry), plain-owned-local bounding anchors (ordering-guarantee wording too thin — revisit with a §28.3 clarification).

#### Migration

Additive except: `Subscribe` handler parameters become `scoped` (existing handler lambdas at call sites are unaffected — the modifier is on the declaration; function-VALUES of the old type held in locals would need the new type, none exist in the corpus).

<a id="sec-v0-175-to-v0-176-changelog"></a>
### v0.176 changelog (v0.175 → v0.176)

v0.176 is the **static-interface-members revision** (#807) — the keystone the spec deferred to by name in four places, closing the design pass's RFC set.

- **Spec §11.8 (new)**: `static` interface members — abstract-only (the §17.4 diamond posture), methods + operators (constants/properties deferred: spell as nullary methods), the C#-style recurrence constraint `where T: I<T>` (no `Self` keyword — deliberately declined: zero new syntax, the recurrence is explicit), `T.Member(...)` and constraint-operator dispatch resolved at instantiation (the compiler already monomorphizes generics; static dispatch uses exactly what specialization has).
- **Compiler-provided primitive conformances** bridging the intrinsic/declared operator split: the numeric tower + `char` conform to the new stdlib §2.19 `INumber<T>`/`ISteppable<T>`/`IParsable<T>` without declaring them; `Parse` is witnessed by the existing per-type members unchanged; for `TryParse`, the per-type members keep their non-nullable value-typed outs (the shape-(c) convention, stdlib §1) and the compiler-provided conformance **bridges the out-nullability** so the constraint surface presents `IParsable<T>.TryParse(out value: T?)` while direct calls keep `out result: T` (v0.184).
- **§16 Range note updated**: the intrinsic element restriction now has its replacement constraint ON RECORD (`ISteppable<T>`), sequenced as a follow-up (no user-visible change).
- **Recorded follow-ups, deliberately not in v0.176**: FromCollectionLiteral → `ICollectionLiteralTarget<T>` and `IDeserializable.Deserialize` promotion (both zero-source-change by design), Range de-intrinsicking, static constants/properties in interfaces, `Self` sugar.

#### Migration

None — purely additive. The §18 deferred-list entry is marked shipped.

<a id="sec-v0-176-to-v0-177-changelog"></a>
### v0.177 changelog (v0.176 → v0.177)

v0.177 is the **call-bounded-default revision** (#1419) — one rule, closing the hole §28.14 left open: what a callee may do with a *plain* function-typed parameter.

- **Spec §28.14 + §28.3 + §22.3**: a function-typed parameter without `scoped` is **call-bounded** — the callee may invoke it, bind it locally, and pass it to other call-bounded parameters, but may not store it in any field or externally-reachable collection, return it, capture it in an escaping closure, or forward it into a `scoped` position (it cannot vouch for captures it cannot see). Compiler-verified for user-authored callees — structural sink checks, no interprocedural analysis; that decidability is the reason this default was chosen over the alternative ("reject caller-side when the callee provably stores"), which needs whole-program facts. The caller side becomes fully unrestricted: any capture-bearing closure is admissible to a plain parameter, bounded by the call.
- **Why plain function values may not be field-stored while plain object borrows may** (the recorded asymmetry): §28.3's borrowed-field rule is structural-check-plus-caller-trust, and for an object borrow the caller can hold that trust — it knows the source. A closure's bound is its capture set, which a plain signature does not carry, so neither party can accept the trust; `scoped` is the signature-carried form of it. No trust without a signature to hang it on.
- **The extension-method-parameter carve-out retires**: subsumed on the caller side by the unrestricted default; the stdlib lazy query operators' retention is stdlib-certified until their signatures migrate to `scoped` (the §30.11 legacy path).
- **Deferred third tier** (#1427): an `unbounded` marker for store/return/compose callees (`Compose(f, g)` is inexpressible over call-bounded parameters) — deferred on the evidence bar; recorded in §28.14.

#### Migration

Caller-side: none — strictly more permissive. Callee-side: user code that stores a plain function-typed parameter must declare it `scoped` (bounded storage) or restructure; the suite triage accompanies the enforcing compiler change (#1419, with the builtin `Subscribe`/`Register` flip #1420).

### v0.178 changelog (v0.177 → v0.178)

v0.178 is the **currency & consistency revision** — the mechanical output of the 2026-07-07 whole-language design review (~140 edits across the five documents; **no semantic rule changes**). Every edit restores agreement where the documents had drifted from decisions already recorded; every defect that required *choosing* between live design alternatives was withheld from this revision and routed to the design-ruling revisions that follow it.

- **Revision-residue sweeps.** The v0.150 discard rule, v0.161 drop-on-overwrite/`TakeCurrent()` redesign, v0.162 `OwningTask<T>.Result` amendment, v0.166 `of` delimiter, v0.169 call-site `owned` markers, v0.170 uniform closers, v0.174 bounded channels, v0.175/v0.177 capture lattice, and v0.176 static interface members are now reflected consistently everywhere they are referenced. Concretely: §28's preamble, disposal-summary table, §28.8, §28.9, and §28.11 no longer state the pre-v0.150/v0.161 rules (the indexer-set/field-assignment "asymmetry" paragraphs described a rule retired three revisions ago); §29.1's destructive-`Current` sentences now describe `TakeCurrent()`; §30.3's prose no longer denies the `Result` member declared seven lines above it; the stranded v0.174 bounded-channels paragraph moved from the head of §31 into §30.15 (only multi-consumer channels remain deferred); three stale `case`-without-`of` examples gained their delimiter; §11.4/§26.1 state the v0.170 closer rule; and stale "deferred" claims for shipped features (concrete serializers v0.115, bounded channels v0.174, static interface members v0.176, the §28.14 `scoped` mechanism) were retired in spec, stdlib, and rationale.
- **Appendix synchronization.** Appendix B now records `of` and `scoped` (B.1 + B.2 rows; `scoped` also joins the reserved-modifier list where the grammar uses it unconditionally); Appendix C.5's async-return invariant admits `OwningTask<T>` and the owning async-iterator forms §30.1 has admitted since v0.162; C.2's accessor-visibility invariant admits the equal-visibility case §13.6 permits; C.1/§11.3 record the cross-kind member-name clash rule the compiler enforces; A.5 gains the parenthesized-function-type production §27.2's prose mandates (with the `?`-binds-to-return-type note); A.7 admits trailing commas in collection literals and corrects the relational-pattern operand level.
- **Ill-formed examples fixed.** §15.4.1's RingBuffer now declares its slot array `owned` (it violated §28.6 as written); §15.1/§15.4 construct records with `new`; §27.8's tuple-type alias — a type form Bezel does not have — was replaced; §17.13 uses the real `FileStream` constructor; §18.5's format-hole example no longer faults under its own delimitation rule; missing v0.169 call-site `owned` markers were added in §29.2/§30.5/§30.11 and stdlib §6.7; §30.8's `Register` example carries the `scoped` marker of erratum #1431; Guide 01's owned-field-read example reflects the v0.151 borrow rule instead of the retired error.
- **Name, anchor, and ordering repairs.** `float`'s wrapper record is `System.Float` — the `Single` name §3.4 reserved never existed in the stdlib; the two stale `Owned*`-convention glosses now read `Owning*` (v0.168, closes the remaining text drift of #1334); §2.1's prose requires module-before-imports, matching grammar A.2 and the compiler; §2.3's blanket "language primitives cannot be shadowed" claim narrowed to §3.4's reserved set (library types such as `Array<T>` and `Subscription` are shadowable, as §3.4 already said); the phantom `end with;` closer left §1.6; roughly thirty dangling or mistargeted intra- and cross-document anchors were repaired (every `sec-*` reference in the three main documents now resolves); the stdlib's §2.18/§2.19 sections returned to file order and its duplicated `Convert` members were removed; §26.5's resolution text now includes the current module in the extension search space and states the ambiguity remedies that actually exist.

No migration: no program changes meaning under this revision. The design review's semantic findings — borrow-liveness composition, async×borrow lifetimes, event-registration capture bounds, statics/initialization rules, nullability-narrowing completeness — land as separate ruled revisions with their own changelogs and tracking issues.

### v0.179 changelog (v0.178 → v0.179)

v0.179 is the **async×borrows settlement revision** — one coherent regime for what holding a borrow across a suspension point means (#1438, #1448, and the general case), plus the §30 rulings that surround it. Where v0.178 restored currency, v0.179 makes the deferred *choices*: every rule below was selected between recorded live alternatives, with the road not taken noted.

- **The core regime (§30.1, §30.13, §9.7): frame capture with a stated trust posture.** An async method's parameters, receiver, and captures live in the heap state-machine frame until the task *settles*, not until the synchronous call returns. Four rules, one shape: (1) **borrow-bearing record parameters and results are forbidden** on async methods/lambdas/iterators (signature-level, post-substitution for generics; #1438's owner ruling of 2026-07-04, landed as drafted) — a raw span window has no checked-mode backstop, so trust is not available there; `CancellationToken` is the single stdlib-certified exception. (2) **Borrow-bearing record locals across a suspension point** require every carried borrow to have a *frame-resident* source — an owned local, `using var`, or `owned` parameter of the same body (#1448, interpretation (a); the owned-field-of-`this` source that §5.15's old text gestured at is deliberately excluded — if `this` dangles the window dangles, backstop-less); suspension points include an async iterator's `yield return`, and the rule extends to **synchronous iterators'** `yield return` (§29.4) — their heap frames have the identical shape, with the consumer free to dispose caller-side sources between `MoveNext` calls. (3) **`owned` parameters transfer into the frame at call time** (the §29.8 counterpart, closing v0.152's recorded deferred piece) and are disposed on every completion path. (4) **Plain class- or interface-typed borrows, `this`, and lambda captures are held until settlement under a normative caller obligation** — *every borrow source reaching an async call must outlive the returned task's settlement* — the same residual-trust shape as §28.3's borrowed-field rule and §28.14's quiescence: structural checks decidable, temporal guarantee the programmer's, `DisposedAccessException` in checked mode, UB unchecked. *Declined: the settlement discipline* (every task holding caller-borrows must be awaited before the sources' scopes exit) — it would outlaw §30.5's own drop idiom and every abandoned instance-method call, a migration far beyond what rationale §5.1's recorded runtime-checked trade-off requires; `TaskScope` provides the settlement guarantee structurally for those who want it, and §30.13's soundness bullet now states the suspension-point interleaving honestly instead of appearing to deny it.
- **The backstop is no longer invisible (§30.10, stdlib §6.7):** in checked disposal mode, a `DisposedAccessException` raised in an abandoned (`using var`-dropped) continuation is reported through the FireAndForget diagnostic channel before being swallowed. *Declined:* logging all abandoned-task faults (noise on legitimate abandonment; the violation signal, not fault traffic, must be loud).
- **Cancellation certification stated (§30.8, §9.7):** the `CancellationTokenSource` must outlive the settlement of every task observing its tokens; the old "this is automatic" sentences are now explicitly conditional cross-references to §30.1's prohibition and its certified exception. *Declined:* a runtime observation cell surviving source disposal.
- **Call-bounded × suspension defined (§28.14):** an async callee's plain function-typed parameter is frame-held to settlement under the §30.1 obligation (capture-bearing closures to async callees stay admissible); the task returned by *invoking* a call-bounded callback inherits the call bound — abandoning it (drop/store/return/FireAndForget without awaiting to settlement) is an escape sink; in a **synchronous callee** the invocation itself is a compile error (a non-`async` body cannot await it — declare the parameter `scoped` or make the callee `async`); fan-out is admitted: tasks accumulated in a purely-local collection discharge via an aggregation-helper await (`await Task.WhenAll(pending)`), per-path. The mis-directed §30.13 cross-reference now points at §30.14. *Declined:* rejecting any callback held across suspension (over-rejects the sound awaiting caller).
- **Deferred-activation frames carry their arguments' borrows (§28.3, §29.4):** iterator/async-iterator factories and lazy query operators produce frames classified as borrow-carrying values; an unbound owned temporary argument is admissible only when the frame is consumed within the same full expression — `Shout(Source(3))` as a loop source is rejected; bind the source first. The **Task family is classified identically**: an owned temporary passed as a plain argument to an async callee whose returned task escapes the full expression (`using var t := SumAsync(Nums(3));`, return, store, FireAndForget) is rejected — the temporary's death at expression end makes the §30.1 violation statically certain, so the reject posture, not the trust posture, applies; in-expression awaits are unaffected. The classification is by declared return type — deliberately conservative, remedy always the one-line bind. *Declined:* C++-style lifetime extension (reopens the recorded reject-not-extend posture; the compiler's current silent acceptance is an unimplemented check, not an extension semantics); *also declined:* trusting escaping-task temporaries under the checked-mode backstop (a checker that can prove the violation must not defer it to runtime).
- **§30 rulings.** *Multi-await:* value-result await consumes only unbound temporaries; named operands are borrow-awaited (multi-await per §30.4) — matches the compiler, deletes the misleading parallels-Pattern-B clause. *Chained slots:* `return await <using-var source>` is a disposal-timing dispensation (deferral to outer-task teardown), not a §28.3 move exception; `return await <owned param>` is an ordinary §28.3 move-out into the chained slot, which switches off the frame's terminal-state disposal for that parameter — the two §30.1/§30.5 rules meet with exactly one disposal. *Fault ownership:* a faulted task owns its exception — exempt from §31.1's dispose-after-arm (the TypeInitializationException pattern), disposed exactly once at task disposal, with in-flight deferral; `SetException`/`TrySetException`/`FromException` now take the exception `owned` (callers with caught borrows chain a fresh cause instead); **aggregates own no fault of their own** — a faulted WhenAll re-raises the first non-successful *input's* owned instance by borrow, so borrowing-aggregator inputs must outlive the aggregate's *consumption*, not just its settlement, and WhenAllOwned retains the faulted input task, disposing it (and the fault, transitively) with the aggregate. *`Task<T>.Result` (Pattern A):* subject to the same owning-location rule as `await`. *WhenAll/WhenAny/WhenAllOwned* gain contracts (all-settle + first-non-success-in-input-order re-raise; empty-WhenAll and empty-WhenAllOwned completed; empty-WhenAny `ArgumentException` raised synchronously at the call site; WhenAllOwned's sketch promoted to contract). *TaskScope* finally appears in §30.10 as the default fan-out posture; the discard idioms are reframed as escape hatches. *Direct `DisposeAsync()`:* physical reclamation runs exactly once after whichever logical-disposal path completes, including when `DisposeAsync` throws.
- **Blocking-acquisition discipline (§30.12, §28.13, stdlib §6.2/§6.3), riding #1362's machinery:** `Mutex`/`Semaphore` `Acquire`/`TryAcquire(timeout)` are compile errors in `async` bodies and raise `InvalidOperationException` where a domain continuation would actually park; startup thread, FFI threads, and immediate acquisitions unaffected. §30.12's stale "FFI-only" claim is replaced by the three legitimate contexts; §28.13's cross-domain idiom becomes `Get().AcquireAsync()`. Framed as pool-starvation/worker-pinning, not §30.3's deterministic deadlock; generalizes #1362 and pre-ratifies proposal 0003's rule 1 for the existing types.
- **Async `Domain.Spawn` entries (§30.14, stdlib §6.8) — proposal 0032's Stage 0, now normative:** nine async rows mirroring the sync rows; the runtime awaits the returned task inside the spawned domain (the async-Main analog); joins track that task, faults surface as `DomainFaultedException`; Task-family returns resolve to the async rows (previously always a sendability error, so no meaning changes).
- **Channel receive abandonment (§30.15, stdlib §6.9):** disposing a pending `Receive` deregisters without consuming; instant-of-disposal handoffs are given back; select/`Receive(token)` stays deferred to the give-back RFC, now listed, with the interim select substitute documented (forwarder tasks merging sources into one channel).
- **Async-iterator holes closed (#1351, §30.7/§29.7):** generated enumerators check their token at every `MoveNextAsync` entry and resume (no implicit body binding — declined as magic); the await-in-finally rule scoped to source-written `finally`; early-abandoned `await using var` locals take §28.12's synchronous-fallback path in §29.7's disposal pass.
- **Runtime-model reconciliation (§30.13, §33.2):** the startup thread runs outside any domain (the #1362 model), which un-contradicts §30.3's escape-hatch paragraph; §33.2 now actually contains the async-Main driving mechanism §30.3 cites.

#### Migration

Compile-time: programs holding a **span (or other borrow-bearing record) across an `await` or a `yield return`** whose source is not frame-resident must re-derive it after the suspension (#1448 — includes iterator bodies, sync and async); the two removed `Stream` async span overloads migrate to the `Array<byte>` windowed forms (#1438); **blocking `Acquire`/`TryAcquire` in async bodies** migrate to `AcquireAsync`/`TryAcquireAsync`; **iterator/query/async composition over owned temporaries** binds the inner source to a local first (`Shout(Source(3))` as a loop source, and `using var t := SumAsync(Nums(3));` — any Task-family call whose task escapes the full expression); a **synchronous callee that invokes a task-returning call-bounded callback** declares the parameter `scoped` or becomes `async`, and any callee **abandoning such a callback's task** (return/store/FireAndForget/bind-and-drop) must await it to settlement — fan-out via a purely-local collection discharged by `await Task.WhenAll` (§28.14); **sourceless `Task<T>.Result` reads on class-typed results** (`SomeProducer().Result`) move the task into an admitted owning position first, exactly as the corresponding `await` must (§30.3); `SetException`/`TrySetException`/`FromException` call sites passing a *named owned* exception add the call-site `owned` marker, and call sites passing a *caught borrow* construct a fresh cause-chained exception. Runtime-visible: none for correct programs — multi-await of named `Task<T>` locals, TCS patterns, and WhenAll/WhenAny behavior are specified to match the implementation; abandoned-continuation `DisposedAccessException` reports appear only in checked disposal mode. The borrowed-inputs-across-suspension obligation is documentation of existing behavior plus a checked-mode backstop, not a new compile error.
