**Types, generics, and inference (fourth train).** (1) §14.5 NEW — generic-method type-argument inference: exact-agreement structural unification (no common-supertype joins), two-phase lambda participation with the closed-slot admission rule (equal or implicitly converting; exact beats converting at ranking), method references via §27.6's exact-preferred ranking (now stated in §27.6 — its OrderBy(Math.Abs) example was previously underivable), target-typed completion (typed declaration/assignment/return/default/determined-argument contexts — codifies the implemented Empty()-factory idiom); explicit lists all-or-nothing; no constructor inference; per-candidate inference before §22.6 with failed candidates silently inapplicable; non-generic beats generic as the LAST comparison, after the v0.181 defaulted-arity tie-break (implemented behavior; C#'s internal order would let a new optional-parameter overload re-route existing calls). (2) §6.6 — compound assignment: desugaring with the target evaluated once (base, member hops, indexes, getter/setter each once; §17.6 becomes an instance) and the checked narrow-integer write-back (b += 10 ≡ b := byte(b + 10), OverflowException on range, runtime RHS admitted); cross-family results (f += 2.5, b += 1.5) are compile errors; ??= and event +=/-= carve-outs restated. (3) §18.5 — nullable holes render null (no dispatch, alignment applies, type-formattability check against non-nullable T); §8.5/§7.4 conformed. (4) §9.8 — records with heap-collection serialized components are ineligible (record-admissibility: value-shaped components only); the v0.182 open question closes as same-treatment (Deserialize is ownership-invalid per §9.7); positional/body records agree; C.8 conformed. (5) §12.2 — blocked-name set is visible-members-only (private never blocks except nested-in-base; internal blocks in-module; cross-module residual stated: distinct members, lookup selects by static type, selected member dispatches per its own virtual-ness); pure liberalization; C.1 conformed. (6) §11.2/§12.1 — scoped joins the exact-match parameter-modifier lists, both directions, with the caller-contract reasoning recorded; C.1 conformed. (7) §17.14 NEW — constant expressions: the closed sublanguage (literals sans interpolation, const/enum refs incl. wrapper constants, nameof, built-in operators over primitives/string, constant conditional, parentheses; default(T) declined-liftable) with compile-time evaluation under runtime semantics and evaluation faults as compile errors; A.8/A.5 grammar comments, §22.12, §17.9 (phantom 'attribute arguments' removed), §5.1, §10.2, §15.1, C.11 re-pointed. (8) §5.1 — reference conversions stated (identity, class→base, →Object with boxing, type→conformed interface, interface→extended, type-parameter→constraint bound, §12.9 variance), ownership carries through unchanged, co-equal ranking (M(Animal)/M(Object) on Dog stays ambiguous; C#'s better-target refinement declined per rationale §14.5); §20/§22.6 conformed. Migration: newly rejected — partial/excess explicit type-argument lists, generic-constructor inference, cross-family compound assignment (previously crashed codegen), scoped mismatches, fault-at-fold const initializers, record collection components (already rejected by impl), converting-only lambda overload sets (previously a silent pick); newly accepted — invisible-base-member name reuse, nullable holes (already implemented). Runtime-visible: none for correct programs.

#### Migration

Compile-time, newly **rejected**: `Dispose()` (or a discard) through a tracked borrow — a borrowed local/parameter (including `this`), a non-owned field read, a call result, a catch or pattern binding, an owning-collection element borrow, or an element read of an `IEnumerable<T>`/enumerator/query-typed source (previously unaddressed; each is a probable bug — restructure so the owner disposes, use the owning collection's removal forms, or iterate the collection itself for the transit regime); assignment to / transfer from / disposal of a captured owned binding inside a lambda (previously admitted by the compiler — restructure to an `owned`-parameter callback); a fresh-producer element of non-trivial-dispose class type in a borrowing-family collection literal (bind the source first, or use the owning family; trivial-dispose elements — nested collection literals — are unaffected); parameter modifiers on operator parameters (previously parseable, semantics undefined); a returned lazy/enumerable/Task-typed frame carrying a scope-bound local's borrow (materialize instead). Newly **warned**: undischarged `owned` parameters of iterators/async methods (adopt with `using var … := owned …` to silence); straight-line use after a dominating dispose/discard is now a mandatory warning. Newly **accepted / defined**, no action needed: `_ := x;` on a named owned binding now has one meaning (announced consume at end of statement); if-expressions and expression-position `case`/`when` over owned arms are defined owned producers (Guide 01's Pattern B shape); returning parameter-sourced lazy pipelines (`Evens(xs) => xs.Where(IsEven)`) is confirmed legal; `cache.Current := c;` through a `set(owned)` setter consumes without a marker; mid-expression producers are defined to be unwind-disposed (no leak on the exception edge — codifies the only sound reading). Runtime-visible: none for correct programs — borrowing-collection `Dispose()` was already specified trivial in §28.9 (the contrary table row promised work no conforming program could observe); the unwind disposal of expression temporaries codifies the behavior three sections already assumed.

*From the statics train:*
Newly **rejected** (compile-time): `this`-observation in a ctor body before the declaring class's §7.9-strict fields are assigned, and in `base(...)`/`this(...)` argument position always; virtual/override/abstract calls on `this` in ctor bodies of non-sealed (or abstract) classes; a within-type forward static-readonly read routed through statically-resolvable calls; `ref`/`out` arguments over owned-state locations or admitted mutable statics; owned-producing non-trivial-dispose default values on plain parameters; capture-bearing member-syntax static-event subscriptions (already implemented, #1542 — now the stated scope). Newly **defined**, no action for correct programs: `out` copy-out semantics (programs observing a partial `out` write in `catch` were relying on unspecified behavior); accessor-target `ref`/`out` bracketing with textual-order write-back; callee-side discharge of assigned-but-unreturned `out owned` values; the construction/static null-watermark + checked-mode `NullReferenceException` residual bounds; self-static-init as ordinary execution (programs that today survive only because the backstop is unimplemented become sanctioned; the `Boot` forward-read shape becomes a compile error). Newly **warned** (should-level): a `static event` member used as a value (alias creation); receiver positions — subscribe family and raise family alike — never warn. **Doc-only:** pattern (a) rewrite; §24.6/§22.9/§22.7-row-2/§28.13-set/warning-independence edits; the B6/B7 conforming restatements (spec §30.14; stdlib §1, §2.16, `TryRead*`, `Mutex.TryAcquire`).

### v0.185 changelog (v0.184 → v0.185)

v0.185 is the **stdlib-coherence & currency batch** — the library-facing settlement of the 2026-07-11 review plus the cross-cutting currency fixes the four v0.184 trains surfaced. No new language rules; it aligns the standard-library document and a set of stale examples/cross-references with the v0.184 ownership-coherence revision.

**Standard library (TRAIN-STDLIB).**
**Standard library (TRAIN-STDLIB).**

- **A third Try shape is sanctioned; `IParsable` witnessing is bridged (stdlib §1, §2.19; spec §11.8; rationale §11.8 rider).** The pervasive concrete-value-typed Try APIs (§9 `TryParse`, `Convert.TryTo*`, §4.14/§4.15 `TryRead*`, `DateTime`/`DateOnly`/`TimeOnly`/`Guid` `TryParse`) declare `bool` + **non-nullable value-typed out** + `default(T)` on false — a shape §1 claimed did not exist ("exactly two … nullable in every form"). §1 now sanctions it as shape **(c)** and opens "three Try shapes", scoping shape (a)'s nullability + `when true` to **generic/class-typed** payloads (where `T?` is unavoidable because `default` of a non-nullable class is a compile error, spec §17.11); the v0.171 uniformity posture targeted generic extraction slots, not always-value-typed families, so shape (c) is not the pre-v0.171 illegal class form. `IParsable<T>.TryParse` keeps `out value: T?` (user class conformers need it) and the **compiler-provided primitive conformances bridge the out-nullability** — generic `T.TryParse(out v)` through the constraint sees `T?`, a direct `int.TryParse(out i)` sees `int`; §2.19's false "no signatures changed" claim is rewritten to state the bridge, and the ambiguous "§11.8" citation in §1 is dropped from the `when true` list (the parse companions are shape (c), which carries no `when true`). *Declined:* migrating every value-typed out to `T?` (breaking, hostile for parse loops, buys no honesty the bool lacks); constraining the interface out to non-nullable `T` (breaks class conformers).
- **Stream async methods are an override surface (stdlib §7.1/§7.2; spec §12.1).** `ReadAsync`/`WriteAsync` are `async virtual` (modifier order per §11.5) with a documented blocking default (delegating to the abstract sync forms — a §30.12 pool-pin, no I/O backstop); `FileStream` and proposal 0006's streams override with real async I/O; memory-backed streams inherit correctly. The span overloads **and** `ReadAll`/`ReadAllAsync` are **fixed base conveniences** — *not* override points (a subclass overriding the windowed/async forms gets the right behavior through them). Under §12.1 (non-virtual-by-default) the prior declarations forbade any override, making genuinely-async I/O unimplementable and contradicting accepted proposal 0006. The §7.1 code fence that swallowed the windowed-form prose and `SeekOrigin` is repaired as part of the edit. *Declined:* `abstract` (boilerplate on memory streams).
- **Reference-implementation and example repairs (stdlib §2.14, §4.5, §4.9, §4.10, §6.1).** The §4.5 `OwningArray` capacity constructor is respelled in valid §20 postfix-conditional syntax (`capacity if capacity > 0 else 1`) and now faults on negative capacity (§1 #1396) instead of silently clamping. The §4.9 `OwningDictionary` `Add`/`PopValue` loops and the §4.10 `pool.Add` example gain the v0.169/v0.180 transfer markers (the `Add` loop's key test moved before the node transfer to avoid a use-after-move the mechanical marker would introduce). The §2.14 cyclic `Node` example declares its spine as `Shared<Node>` and its back-edge `owned Back: Weak<Node>?` (was a plain owned edge that could not anchor the `Weak` back-edge and tripped §9.8's lint); the §2.14 `Order`/`Invoice` examples gain component-binding primary constructors (the prior constructors bound no owning components — a §9.8 constructor-selection compile error and a §7.9 violation). The §6.1 linked-source idiom binds its `WithCancelAfter` source to a named `using var` (the prior unbound temporary cancelled the link on disposal).
- **Sendability, disposal, retention, and container-contract prose (stdlib §5, §4.4/§4.8/§4.10, §6.3/§6.4/§6.9, §6.5, §6.6, §7.1/§7.2).** §6.3 `Semaphore` and §6.4 atomics are stated **sendable** (the spec delegated this statement to §6.2–§6.4, but §6.3 said nothing); §6.9's "only Mutex + Channel" sentence is widened to the full sendable set. `destructor;` declarations are added to `EventSource`/`AsyncEventSource`, `Channel`/`ChannelSender`, `TaskCompletionSource`/`OwningTaskCompletionSource` (source-owns-task disposal, spec §30.11), and `FileStream` (whose flush-on-dispose contract was previously stated nowhere), and Stream's abstract-disposal caveat is stated — under §1 the absence had meant no-op. §5 states the **callback-taking** lazy operators' callback-retention certification (spec §28.14 named it; §5 had no retention text), explicitly excluding the callback-free lazy operators. §4.4/§4.5/§5 gain a sorting contract (stability per API, total-order comparer, throw-edge element preservation, re-entrancy → `InvalidOperationException`); §4.8/§4.10 gain the store-time key/element stability rule and the `Set`/`OwningSet` iteration-order decision (Set insertion-ordered, OwningSet no guarantee).

**Currency & consistency batch (TRAIN-EDIT).**
**Currency & consistency batch (post-v0.184 seam sweep).** Twenty-two mechanical edits closing stale-text and dangling-reference seams the v0.179/v0.180/v0.183/v0.184 trains left, none of them design changes. §10.6's canonical enum-matching example moves from the retired comma-alternative spelling to `|` (v0.167). §12.6's FileSource.LoadAsync is rewritten to the real `File.ReadAllTextAsync(_path): Task<string>` (removing an invented 1-arg `FileStream` ctor and a `ReadAllAsync`/`Task<string>` type mismatch), and the four remaining 1-arg `FileStream` construction examples (§21.6, §28.10 ×2, §31.2) take the real `(path, FileMode.Open)` ctor. Appendix C.10's enum co-declaration bullet is conformed to §25.2's v0.183 wording (a plain `GetHashCode(): int` on enums, which never carry `override`). §17.6's owned-field `++`/`--` paragraph is rewritten onto §28.7 drop-on-overwrite (result produced first, displaced value disposed implicitly, no warning), replacing pre-v0.161 must-dispose-first/must-warn text. §7.4's 'how narrowing is established' enumeration and §12.1's override modifier-match list each gain the v0.183 `when true`/`when false` out-postcondition (§22.4), which their own prose and §22.4's back-citation already presumed present. §28.3's move-semantics enumeration, discharge-form list, and `??` producers row each gain `throw` (already an announced kill in §31.1 and the freeze boundary, previously unlisted in these three enumerations). Rationale §11.3 is corrected to the `|` catch-alternative spelling; rationale §12.1's awaiter-borrow prose is broadened from 'must be held in `using var`' to the current §30.5 admitted-owning-location set, and 'the only syntactic shape that compiles' becomes 'the canonical shape' (post-v0.89 loosening). The phantom 'module-level method/helper' phrasing — Bezel has no free functions (rationale §11.3: a `public static class` is the free-function surface) — is corrected to 'static method on a static class' at spec §26.3, §26.5 rule 4, and rationale §18. Finally, Appendix C gains three invariants that exist normatively but were unlisted: the §22.4 out-postcondition (C.5), and the §31.2.1 multi-type-catch nearest-common-base-above-Object and generic-catch-arm class-bound rules (C.7). Migration: none — every edit is doc-only currency; no correct program's meaning changes.

### v0.186 changelog (v0.185 → v0.186)

v0.186 is the **shared-state & data-parallelism graduation** — accepted proposals 0003 (`Locked<T>`/`RwLocked<T>`) and 0032 (parallel extensions, stages 0–1.5) land in the normative documents as one composed revision (the two edit the same §22.12/§28.13/§30.12/§30.14 passages; #1703). All open design questions were resolved by delegated rulings recorded here and in §12.8/§12.9; the owner reviews on the tracking issues.

**Data-owning locks (TRAIN-LOCK; proposal 0003 → spec §30.12 "Data-owning locks", §22.12 rule 4, §28.13, §30.13 edge 1, §30.14; stdlib §6.11; rationale §12.8).**

- `Locked<T>`/`RwLocked<T>`: the lock owns its interior; guard `Value` is a guard-sourced borrow (the `Shared.Get()` dispensation), so the `using var` scope is the critical section with zero new lifetime machinery. Interior admission **reuses the sendable derived property** (`T` must be a sendable class type, checked at instantiation) — the precise form of 0003's "transfer-closed interior", no new predicate. Full acquisition surface mirrors `Mutex` (blocking/`Try(timeout)`/`Async(token)`/`TryAsync`), inheriting the v0.179 blocking discipline. Non-reentrancy stated — including `Mutex`'s, previously unstated anywhere — plus the rwlock recursive-read hazard (a second `Read()` may queue behind a waiting writer; fairness unspecified). Locks sendable; guards not. Guard release joins §30.13 edge 1 (rwlock refinement stated in §30.12; the edge's acquisition-form list extended). Guard-across-`await` is a should-level lint, not a ban.
- **Guard-liveness checks (new checking rules, counted).** §28.3's announced-kill carve-out is justified by the killed object's own disposed-flag backstop; a guard kill sets no flag on the *interior* its surviving borrows reference while releasing the lock — so the carve-out does not extend to guards (the §28.14 admission-freeze precedent): explicit `Dispose()`/discard of a guard binding under a live `Value`-sourced borrow is a compile error, and a live guard counts as a live borrow of the lock binding it came from (body-local kills of the lock under a live guard are rejected the same way). Cross-body/cross-domain lock destruction under outstanding guards takes the §28.2 posture, stated normatively: checked-mode deterministic fault (destruction with live guards detected; stale guard access → `DisposedAccessException`), unchecked UB.
- **Read guards are write-restricted (new checking rule, counted; scope stated honestly).** Concurrent cross-domain read guards are the type's point, and Bezel has no read-only borrow — so **within the body holding the guard**, through a `ReadGuard`-sourced borrow every store, `move`, and `ref`/`out` pass is a compile error (expression-site, borrow-provenance-keyed, the v0.184 dispose-through-borrow family; body-local because borrow provenance does not cross calls). The **recorded residual** (§30.14 indirect-alias genus): mutating methods invoked through the read borrow, and any callee reached with the read borrow as a plain argument. *Declined:* deferring `RwLocked`; pure residual trust; per-interior read facades; a const-method vocabulary (§12.5's road; lift path: a read-only view form designed with the frozen-view family).
- **Static membership, recast on v0.184's ground (recorded deviation from 0003's letter).** 0003's "join the rule-2 form-(i) set" predates v0.184's store semantics: a mutable static lock would be *sound* under them, but overwrite-never-disposes would leak a displaced lock plus its whole interior (payload-scaled, unlike the `Task?` cache), and racing first-use stores could transiently fork a registry into two lock instances. No use case demands lock-slot reassignment (mutability lives behind the guards), so the locks join **rule 4's new v0.186 suppression list** — the `static owned readonly` registry, 0003's actual deliverable, is warning-free and exit-disposed — and stay **out of form-(i)** (mutable lock statics rejected). Liftable by separate ruling. Both lock types join §28.13's `Shared`-payload set by separate ruling per its no-silent-growth clause (`Shared<Locked<T>>` is the `Shared<Mutex>` idiom with the state attached).

**Parallel extensions, stages 0–1.5 (TRAIN-PAR; proposal 0032 → spec §30.14 "Data-parallel combinators", §30.15, §28.13, §28.14, §22.12 rule 4, §28.3, §28.11, §30.1; stdlib §4.19, §6.9, §6.12; rationale §12.9).**

- **Stage 0** was already normative (v0.179 async spawn entries; impl tracker #1523) — cross-referenced, not re-landed. Its rider lands now: **`Channel<T>.ReceiveAll()`**, the non-exceptional drain form (`await for` over the §30.7 interfaces; completes normally on drained-and-closed; one consumption in progress — a second `ReceiveAll`, a `ReceiveAll` begun over a pending `Receive`, or interleaved receives raise `InvalidOperationException`; affine per §29.11; abandonment deregisters like `Receive`). Zero new checking rules.
- **Stage 1**: compiler-known `Parallel.Map`/`Reduce`/`ForEach` over a lazy process-wide worker-domain team. The bodies are **spawn positions** — one table extension of the existing call-site category (§28.14's list names them); zero new checking rules (thesis re-verified against the v0.184 capture/freeze changes: capture-free entries are unaffected). Snapshot-at-call (run-to-completion makes it a contract); results in input order; first-fault-wins as `DomainFaultedException` (*declined:* a `ParallelFaultedException` carrying the failing index — message text suffices, a subclass is additive later); moved-in unprocessed items disposed (the channel-close precedent); call→body and body→settlement visibility derived from the §30.13 edges (the "five edges" title stays true). Returns follow the `Domain.Spawn` owned-task convention (noted against §6.7's unmarked `WhenAll` rows — deliberate, not to be silently harmonized). **`Reduce` seed semantics stated plainly** (new): per-worker fold from `seed`, partials combined in an unspecified tree — a non-identity seed is incorporated once per worker; associativity documented, not checked. `degree: int := 0` = `DefaultDegree` (= `ProcessorCount` at team creation, fixed per process); negative raises `ArgumentException`. *Recorded deferrals:* async bodies, class-element `Reduce`, cancellation parameter, user-declared spawn positions.
- **Stage 1.5**: `FrozenArray<T>` (stdlib §4.19) — deeply immutable, fixed-size; `T` restricted to sendable value types and `string` (intrinsic, the `Atomic<T>` style); `From(owned OwningBuffer<T>)` O(1) steal (value-typed only; *declined:* a receiver-consuming `Freeze()`, which would need a receiver-consumption mechanism the language does not have) and copying `From(Array<T>)` (the only string form). Sendable (§30.14 row). **Membership rulings under v0.184's no-silent-growth clause** (the recast of 0032's q4 — no definitional widening of "internally synchronized" is needed or made): joins the §28.13 `Shared`-payload set as its first **deep-immutability** member (reads need no machinery; reclamation synchronization is `Shared<T>`'s own atomic control block — #689, implemented — plus the string-precedent storage tolerance); joins §22.12 rule 4's suppression list; deliberately **not** form-(i) (the same payload-leak ground as the locks). The §28.13 set's relation to form-(i) is restated (minus `ChannelSender<T>`, plus the three v0.186 members). `Parallel.*` gains zero-copy `Shared<FrozenArray<A>>` overloads (one handle cloned per worker).
- **Freeze-time aliasing closed honestly (rulings, counted).** `FrozenArray`'s "no writer can exist" is delivered by named rules plus one named obligation, not by assumption: (1) the consume-site freeze now **states** that a live borrow-bearing-record local (a span) counts as a live local borrow of its carried sources (§28.3 — making normative what §9.7's subjection of record values to §28.3's borrow rules already implied; a span local over a buffer freezes it against `From(owned …)` and every other consume); (2) the v0.180 **domain clause is extended** at its recorded attachment points (§28.3 borrowed-field rule — the single full statement — §28.11's store rule, §30.1's settlement obligation by reference, the §28.3 fields-not-frozen note, §30.14's summary): the caller-side obligation now also covers **consuming a borrowed-from source into a domain-reachable construction** — `FrozenArray<T>.From`, the `Shared<T>`/`Locked<T>`/`RwLocked<T>` constructors, an admitted static store — which is not a domain transfer but publishes the storage cross-domain while the borrow survives (field/slot-sourced consumes are freeze-exempt and dispose nothing, so no conformance mode can catch this route). For pre-v0.186 payload types the newly-named shapes were benign (the payload was itself synchronized).
- **Stage 2 recorded, not landed (rationale §12.9)**: blocked-primary `Parallel.Join` (the awaiting variant recorded as weaker and more novel); `concurrently-readable` (§3.6 form, fork-position-checked; locks/channels/tasks excluded); the fork-extent acquisition guard **widened to cover the new §6.11 locks**; provenance-linear `SplitAt` witnesses with **opaque lending by type** (a lend-span family; the interprocedural body rule declined); `par` as a compiler-known-only contextual modifier (no grammar reservation in this revision); the location-granular §30.14 invariant amendment ratified in principle, pinned verbatim, deliberately *not* applied now (nothing in v0.186 violates the current sentence); the rule-4-statics fork residual sharpened (a confinement-honoring program can newly race through its own forks — the landing must address it explicitly). *Declined, binding:* a `parallel for` statement; move-capturing spawn bodies; user-generic parallel libraries; a runtime send-check. `.AsParallel()` stays a recorded endnote (§29.11 affinity removes PLINQ's hazard class structurally; evidence first).

**FFI v2 graduation (proposal 0033 + the `env` extension).** Accepted proposal 0033 (owner, 2026-07-12) landed in full (its Stages A+B+C), together with the six §32 defect amendments 0033 §0 had routed to earlier trains that shipped without them (routing corrected; re-verified against v0.185), and one owner-requested extension designed at graduation: **capture-bearing call-bounded callbacks (the `env` clause)**, answering the owner's instance-callback question ("marshal an object method that can update the class object it comes from"). §32 grows from a calling convention into an FFI: foreign memory, C-compatible records, boundary `out`/`ref`, symbol aliases and C-variadic imports, typed handles — every addition **trusted but unverified** in §32's existing sense, explicit at the call site, with the dangerous operations named as dangerous and confined behind `import System.Interop`.

- **Foreign memory (§32.12; stdlib §10.5, §10.1–§10.3, §4.14).** `Ptr<T>` — typed, element-scaled, named-methods-only foreign access; `IntPtr` stays opaque *placement*. Pointee set gated per-instantiation; `Ptr<Ptr<U>>` declined (v1); `Ptr<T>` sendability ratified with a cross-domain UB trust bullet (§32.10). `RawBytes.FromForeign` (view or `free(3)`-on-dispose); `CString`/`WString.Pointer`; `OwningBuffer<T>.DangerousPointer()` (value-typed presentation only — the class-typed presentation can never satisfy the gate). The **no-object-address invariant** stated: class references never convert to addresses. *Declined:* Marshal-style untyped reads; checked foreign memory; operator pointer arithmetic (rationale §16.3).
- **C-compatible records (§32.13; §3.6).** New derived-property row + the language's **first representation promise** (target-C-ABI layout, declaration order, ABI padding), scoped to classified records; §3.6's behavior-dispatch reservation gains its single scoped exception, ratified together with the promise (rationale §16.5). By-address admission (`ref`/`out`, `Ptr<R>`); single-integer/pointer-field records pass directly (typed handles — `Sqlite3Db` vs `Sqlite3Stmt` confusion becomes a compile error); wrapper classes remain the lifetime answer (`closes` clause declined, rationale §16.7). By-value structs stay Stage-D-deferred (§32.14). Unions/bitfields declined with recorded workarounds.
- **Boundary `out`/`ref` (§32.5, new sub-block).** Direct address-of-caller-storage semantics, normative (re-entrant callbacks can observe mid-call writes — through statics, derived `Ptr`s, or a captured `ref` argument of the same call); `out`'s definite assignment granted at return with the write trusted (§32.10 bullet); **new compile error**: a callback argument of an extern call may not capture a binding passed `out` to the same call (indeterminate-bits observation, statically checkable). `out owned`/`owned`/string-type `ref`/`out` not admitted, with reasons. Closes the accepted-but-miscompiled modifier surface.
- **RawBytes marshalling pinned (§32.5)** — previously "a pointer-and-length pair" with no C shape: parameter positions occupy **two consecutive C slots** (pointer, then length); `RawBytes` extern returns are **rejected** (no return convention for two slots; wrap via `FromForeign`); `RawBytes?` marshals NULL/0. (0033 §6.2 named this hole; it does not survive the graduation.)
- **Symbol binding (§32.11, repurposed; the old reserved list moves to §32.14 keeping its anchor).** Identifier-is-the-symbol stated; `:= symbol "…"` aliases; §32.3's bare-name derivation promoted to a stated rule; **startup resolution pinned** — every resolution failure surfaces before `Main`, lazy binding conforming only if it preserves that observable failure point, with the fail-fast cost recorded (platform-absent symbols make a linking program fail at startup until 0034-era conditionals exist); `variadic(N)` with the promoted-type compile error and the fixed-arity-binding `%al` UB warning; true varargs declined (rationale §16.6).
- **Callbacks (§32.8).** Exception escape now **aborts with a diagnostic** (was platform-dependent; never unwinds native frames). Execution context defined: a callback invoked **on the thread executing the extern call** is ordinary code of the calling continuation; an invocation on any other thread — *including during the call* (parallel native callees) — is a foreign-thread invocation (confinement for plain callbacks; UB with a checked-mode guard for `env`-paired ones). **NEW — the `env` clause**: an extern declares its C user-data slot (`env` marker) and that slot's position in the callback's C signature (`env` position in the function type); the paired callback parameter becomes **capture-admitting** — bound instance-method references and capturing lambdas included — under §28.14's call-bounded caller rule, callee obligations documented-trusted (§32.10: same-window, same-thread, env passed through, nothing retained), compiler-synthesized trampoline, checked-mode thread guard specified as a per-activation environment-block record (temporal axis recorded as guardless; QoI poisoning permitted), environment lifetime = the extern call, no retained pair mintable. `sqlite3_exec` rows now land in `this` directly. **Retained callbacks** get the documented registry idiom (static callback + integer token + `Locked<OwningDictionary<…>>`, proposal 0003): graceful-miss-not-UAF by construction, with the **teardown discipline stated** (destructor-side blocking `Lock()` inherits §30.12's park→`InvalidOperationException` backstop; async disposal path or outside-domain disposal are the safe shapes; guarantee process-lifetime-bounded). `Interop.CodeAddress<F>` mints process-lifetime addresses of static-admissible callbacks (one-way; §28.14 explicitly exempted, not silently violated). *Declined:* reusing `scoped` at the boundary; a `GetFunctionPointerForDelegate`-style retained-thunk intrinsic; `ForeignHandle<T>` (deferred, rationale §16.7).
- **§0 defect amendments folded in:** `owned CString?` return alignment (§32.1/§32.6); nullable boundary forms admitted, nullable value types outlawed (§32.5); the errno example made real over `Interop.LastErrno` with the read-first/never-across-await window (§32.9; stdlib §10.6); inline-array write-back defined, `[N]T` returns rejected, element set extended to pointer-sized scalars — parameters and record fields uniformly, one recorded step past 0033 §4.1's letter, and the unmarked-by-address passing recorded against the §22.3 marker doctrine (rationale §16.5); foreign-thread runtime obligations pinned **including the in-callback allocation question: allocation is available on foreign threads** (§32.10); blocking-extern domain-stall documented (§32.10).
- **Module homes (stdlib §10; spec §2.3/§4.8):** §10.0–§10.4 boundary types declared to live in auto-imported `System`; `Ptr<T>`/`Interop` in explicitly-imported `System.Interop` (the import line is the foreign-memory audit marker).
- **Grammar/appendices:** extern grammar gains `ExternParamList`/`ExternParam` (`env` marker, two-token lookahead documented), the `:= symbol` clause and `VariadicClause`; `symbol`/`variadic`/`env` join **both** Appendix B.1 enumerations and the B.2 table (the `env` row states the parameter-name and type-shadowing corners); Appendix C.9 gains the FFI invariant rows; Appendix D.2's FFI row gains its stdlib column. §28.14's interaction paragraph names the boundary instance of the call-bounded default (and its `[§32]` link is repaired from `#sec-ffi` to the §32 anchor — editorial).

**Migration.** Compile-time, newly **rejected**: every new rule governs v0.186 API surface (`Locked<Dictionary<…>>`-style non-sendable interiors, read-guard stores, guard kills under live borrows, mutable statics of the three suppression-list types), with one reach-back stated explicitly: consuming a binding while a live span local over it survives is now explicitly within the consume-site freeze (§28.3) — programs relying on that shape were already unsound under §9.7's umbrella rule. Newly **defined**: everything above; `ReceiveAll` is the sanctioned drain idiom (the `catch ChannelClosedException` loop remains legal). Newly **warned** (should-level): a lock guard live across `await`. **Recorded obligations** (not compiler-checked): reader purity beyond stores through `ReadGuard<T>.Value` (mutating methods; callees reached with the read borrow as a plain argument — spec §30.12); the extended domain clause (consumption into domain-reachable constructions — spec §28.3/§30.14); no guard outliving its lock across domains (spec §30.12). **Doc-only:** the §28.13 set-relation restatement; the §30.12 three-places widening; §28.14's spawn-position list naming `Parallel`; `Mutex` non-reentrancy stated; Appendix C's rule-4 bullet updated. Spec-ahead-of-impl trackers filed at landing: §6.11 locks + guard-liveness checks, §6.12 combinators/team, §4.19 `FrozenArray` (+#689 machinery verification), §6.9/§30.15 `ReceiveAll`, §28.3 freeze-sees-span-locals. Stage 2's gate issue supersedes the Stage-2 half of #1510. Newly **rejected** (compile-time): nullable value types in extern signatures (previously accepted, no C representation); `[N]T` and `RawBytes` extern returns; rvalue inline-array extern arguments; `owned`/`out owned`/string-type `ref`/`out` extern parameter forms (previously parseable; `out` miscompiled); capture of a same-call `out` argument by a callback argument; capture-bearing callbacks at *unpaired* extern parameters keep being rejected, now with a remedy-naming diagnostic. Newly **defined**: callback exceptions abort with a diagnostic (programs relying on platform swallow behavior were relying on unspecified behavior); synchronous-callback execution context; boundary `out`/`ref` semantics; `RawBytes` two-slot parameter marshalling; foreign-thread runtime surface (allocation available; async-signal context narrower); blocking-extern domain stall; symbol-resolution failure timing (before `Main`). Newly **accepted**: `env`-paired capture-bearing callbacks (incl. bound instance-method references); `ref x`/`out var x`/`out _` at extern call sites; `owned` extern returns (`owned CString?`); `variadic(N)` imports and `:= symbol` aliases; C-compatible records by address; single-field handle records (incl. variadic positions — recorded extension); `Ptr<T>` and the new stdlib members (`FromForeign`, `Pointer`×2, `DangerousPointer`, `LastErrno`, `CodeAddress`). Doc-only: module-home statements, the §3.6 row + scoped reservation exception, D.2's FFI row, §32.11→§32.14 renumbering (old anchor preserved at §32.14; all inbound links resolve to the deferred list they meant). Runtime-visible for correct programs: none — every change is additive or defines previously-undefined boundary behavior. The guides teach no FFI idiom; no guide revalidation is triggered (pins untouched).

### v0.187 changelog (v0.186 → v0.187)

**The `event` member kind is retired (proposal 0035, accepted 2026-07-12; #1550).** An event is now the stdlib §6.5 pattern — a `private owned readonly` `EventSource<T>` field plus a public `IEvent<T>` borrowing property — with subscriber-side call sites unchanged. Removed: `EventDecl`/`IfaceEvent` (A.4), §24.3's two-faced member typing (the language's only access-site-dependent member-type rule), §24.1's placement/modifier rules (dissolved into §9.7 and the ordinary member grammars), §28.14 form 4's event-backing-member clause, and §22.12 rule 5's member-kind keying. §24's semantics relocate to stdlib §6.5 sentence-by-sentence (snapshot-raise; RaiseAsync sequencing verbatim; first-error-wins, cancellation-as-fault, no-aggregation; the raising-domain rule; the construction-window caveat with its §22.7 cite; per-type thread safety including the distinct FFI clause; quiescence) — one wording correction recorded (former §24.5's "same posture as §29.12" becomes the contrasting-response statement, rationale §13.6); §24 itself becomes a tombstone section carrying its old anchors (no renumbering of §25–§33). The `+=`/`-=` desugaring is kept, re-homed to §17.2 and extended to `SharedEventSource<T>`, with its `readonly`-LHS interaction stated for the first time (the desugaring is recognized before `readonly`-assignability checking). Statics: the sealed `ISharedEvent<out T>` + `SharedEventSource<T>` pair replaces `static event` — internally synchronized, capture-free at every subscription site: the admission is a stdlib-stated entry in §28.14's capture-free register keyed on the resolved callee (constrained-generic receivers included), the pair deliberately does not implement `IEvent<T>`, and — new, register-wide — method-reference formation over a capture-free-register position is a compile error (covering `Domain.Spawn` too, closing the same latent formation hole there), which together close **#1647 by construction**; rule 5 restates enforceably on the types; the v0.184 interim static-event text (member-syntax scoping, the #1647 residual, the value-use warning, the backing-field accounting sentence, §24.6's static exception, §30.14's static-event clause, C.11's two static-event bullets) is superseded. `SharedEventSource<T>` joins §22.12 rule 2's form-(i) set (C.11's enumeration follows) and is expressly excluded from §28.13's `Shared`-payload set (the relation clause now names both exclusions). A new callee-side borrow rule lands with the train (§28.3/§28.6): a bare `static` `owned`-field read returned through a non-`owned` return is a borrow of process-lived static storage — the rule the pattern's static property face needed (previously only the caller-side producers row existed). `EventSource<T>`/`AsyncEventSource<T>` gain public parameterless constructors (#1646 tracks the compiler; sequenced first — the pattern is the graduation's front door); the six event types join §2.3's always-available names (the Q7 posture reversal is recorded in §13.6); `event` moves from B.1 to B.3 as the language's one reserved-for-future identifier. *Declined, with reasons recorded in §13.6:* option (a) expansion sugar and its bare-name variant; the alternative declaration surfaces C3–C10; deleting the desugaring (would close #1618 by deletion but churn every producer site — #1618 stays open); S2/S3 statics; the shared async twin (deferred — `static async event` has no direct replacement until it ships; the channel bridge is the alternative); the transparent-getter form-4 hop (recorded liftable — tracking issue T4). *Findings dissolved rather than patched:* seam-audit-04, spec-hot-04. **Migration:** every `event` declaration — class, interface, `static`, `async` — is a reserved-word error, with stdlib §6.5's pattern as the replacement spelling (interface events → `readonly property E: IEvent<T>;`; static events → the `SharedEventSource<T>` idiom with capture-free handlers at every site); producer-side call sites re-spell to the field (`_e.Raise(…)`, `_e += h`, `_e -= h`); subscriber-side call sites are byte-for-byte unchanged; off-idiom capture-bearing external subscriptions whose `Subscription` is discharged neither by `using var` (form 2) nor into an `owned` field of `this` (form 3) are newly rejected (diagnostic remedy: bind the subscription with `using var`); a capture-bearing handler at any shared-source subscribe position, and method-reference formation over any capture-free-register position, are compile errors; rule 5's v0.184 should-warn on static-event value uses retires with the hazard it flagged.

### v0.188 changelog (v0.187 → v0.188)

**Module identity, artifact interface, and program assembly — spec §2.8 (proposal 0034 graduated; tracking #1517).** The back half of §2 — everything downstream of a single compilation, previously an honor system — is now written, as four rulings plus a non-goals list, with consistency edits to §2.1/§2.4/§2.5/§2.6/§13.4/§27.8/§33.1/§33.5/§33.6 and Appendix C (C.12 updated, C.13 added). Proposal 0034's open questions 1–8 are resolved per the proposal's own recommendations as delegated rulings (owner acceptance 2026-07-12 delegated them).

- **§2.8.1 Module identity and closure.** A module is the product of exactly one compilation; membership is fixed by the files presented to it — no file joins a module by declaring its name, and `internal` is closed by compilation (SCC co-members see nothing of each other's internals; §13.4/§2.1 amended to match). Duplicate module names across **distinct** artifacts are a build error naming both origins — the metadata-time diagnostic is the normative standard (OQ2), link-time discovery conforming-but-substandard — while bit-identical duplicate presentations (the diamond-assembly case) are deduplicated, not diagnosed. Self-import is a compile error (rejecting both the tautological-no-op reading, which would perturb §2.2 collision arithmetic, and the compiler's accidental publics-only third semantics). The standard-library modules are **implementation-provided**: exempt from artifact presentation, but inside duplicate-name detection — `module System;` in user code becomes a build error instead of a silent namespace grab. *Declined:* silent merge (the encapsulation hole), first/last-wins (silent re-meaning, exactly what §2.7 excludes at the name level).
- **§2.8.2 The artifact interface is a semantic requirement.** §2.5's closed three-item metadata list was false to the language (monomorphized generics need bodies); it is replaced by a capability statement: the interface must let a consumer type-check the public (and, for cross-module derivation, `protected` — OQ8) surface including derived-type-property verdicts/structural facts (§3.6), instantiate public generics at external arguments with semantics identical to same-module instantiation, and identify/describe dependencies keyed by program-wide identity. Definition-site visibility for carried generic bodies is stated, with its honest cost (internals reached by exported generic bodies become binary interface; a staleness error, not a compatibility trap, under the recompile-the-world model). **No restrictions beyond visibility** (OQ6): an implementation unable to carry a body shape must reject with a diagnostic naming the shape (the #710-style diagnosed gate is a conforming interim), never silently diverge (#1222's shape is nonconforming). Source-text embedding — what the reference compiler ships — is a legitimate format under the rule.
- **§2.8.3 Transitive dependencies and cross-artifact type identity.** The build supplies the transitive closure, including modules referenced only from carried declaration bodies; a missing member is a named build error (metadata-time diagnosis the intended standard). The **naming/use split** (OQ3): values of transitively-reachable types may be used — received into inferred bindings, called, passed, returned, disposed — without import; every source-spelled naming (type ascription, `new`, cast, type test, `catch`, explicit generic argument, extension declaration) requires importing the declaring module. *Declined:* import-required-for-everything (breaks composition — even compiler-inserted disposal of a returned value would be illegal), everything-without-import (floods the bare-name space, makes §2.2 collision arithmetic closure-dependent). Program-wide type identity is `(declaring module, qualified name, arity)` (constructed generics: the generic plus its arguments); all descriptions of one type must agree — disagreement (a stale artifact) is a named build error instead of today's silent ABI garbage (#1487). And identity is one type **at runtime**: one static state, one recorded initialization (§22.12 rule 1, §22.13), one runtime type identity per instantiation per process, no matter how many compilations emitted its monomorphized code (#1513 is the evidence bug; duplicate code copies are permitted only where observationally indistinguishable).
- **§2.8.4 Program assembly.** Artifact kind (executable/library) is chosen by the **build request**, not inferred from `Main`-presence (OQ4 — a recorded deviation from the design dive's sketch: inference silently flips a build's kind in both directions; implementations may still offer inference as tooling convenience). The **main module** is redefined as *the module containing the selected entry point*, **superseding v0.181's definition by build-target**; entry-point search scope is the whole **root compilation** (OQ5, ratified widening: for a several-module root SCC every member's classes are searched — v0.181's letter excluded SCC co-members and needed a build-target tie-break §2 no longer requires). A qualifying `Main` in a dependency artifact is **inert** — v0.181's decline of *program-wide* search stands: adding a dependency can never break, change, or steal an entry point (#1511's `multiple definition of 'main'` becomes a spec violation on the `-c` path). Dependency artifacts must be library-kind (an executable presented as a dependency is a kind error). Link mode (static embed vs. dynamic) is implementation-defined under the **one-copy-per-process** guarantee: one copy of each module's code, one static state and one runtime identity per type including per generic instantiation. Static-init cycle rejection across units needs interface-carried dependency edges; that metadata clause is deferred to the #804 lane (OQ7) rather than blocking §2.8.
- **§2.8.5 Non-goals**, each now a recorded decline: package management/versioning/registries; ABI stability across recompilation; conditional compilation (one source text, one meaning — concurring with stdlib-gap-review-2026-07 declined item 6, which routed the question here); selective imports; re-exports; wildcard imports. Revisiting any requires new evidence against the stated reason.

*Migration:* newly **rejected** — two distinct artifacts declaring one module name; a user file declaring an implementation-provided module name (`module System;`); self-import; presenting an executable artifact as a dependency. Newly **defined** — artifact-interface capability (§2.5's parenthetical list replaced), transitive-closure supply, program-wide and runtime type identity (staleness = named error), root-compilation entry-point scope — for a several-module root SCC this **widens** the v0.181 single-module search (semantic change, ratified). **Doc-only** (codifying current compiler behavior) — the naming/use split, metadata-driven type-checking of imports, static-embed link mode, explicit build-request kinds, `-c` needing no `Main`. Impl trackers: evidence bugs #1487, #1488, #1489, #1511, #1513, #1514 stay open with new citations; #804 (static-init dependency metadata) and #1398 (SCC build driver) unchanged; new issues filed at landing for duplicate-module/stdlib-name detection, self-import rejection, metadata-time closure diagnostics, derived-property carriage, executable-as-dependency kind check, and entry-point scope.

**Object-initializer blocks retired — `with` means record update, only (proposal 0037 graduated; tracking #1648).** `new T(args) with ... end` on a **class** type — by §22.11's own former "Equivalent to", pure sugar for binding the instance to a local and assigning public settable members in textual order — is deleted, and with it the language's one type-kind-dispatched expression semantics: one spelling that meant *copy-with-overrides* on a record source and *setter mutation on a fresh instance* on a class source, a dispatch invisible at the call site. Rulings and edits:

- **§9.5 states one meaning plus one rejection.** A `with` expression requires a **record-typed source**; a class-typed source is a compile error naming the rule, with a diagnostic teaching both remedies — named/optional constructor arguments (§22.5), which run the constructor and respect its invariants, first; bind-then-assign second (delegated ruling per proposal 0037 Q2). The discriminator is the source expression's type kind, never the presence of `new`: `new Point(1, 2) with Y := 9 end` remains ordinary record `with` on the freshly-constructed value — the resolution rule formerly in §22.11's closing paragraph, now stated in §9.5. The three-uses keyword note shrinks to two (record update; `await for ... with token`), losing the only pair that needed the type checker to tell apart.
- **§22.11 is tombstoned, not renumbered** (delegated ruling per proposal 0037 Q3): §22.12 static members is heavily cited and must not shift. The tombstone names the replacement idioms and the dissolution of the construct-specific disposal rule.
- **§22.9 loses a dangling analogy.** The chaining-constructor body-throw case was defined "the same rule §22.11 applies"; its own sentence already states the rule standalone (fully-initialized instance disposed through the normal generated-`Dispose()` path before the exception propagates), so only the citation is deleted. No semantic change.
- **No grammar-production change** — the `with` PrimarySuffix and `InitAssign` stay: `new Record(...) with ... end` (legal) and `new Class(...) with ... end` (now rejected) are syntactically identical, so no production can separate them; the restriction is a type-checker rule, the same over-admit-and-reject-semantically pattern as Appendix A.4's notes. The "cleaner grammar split" idea is recorded as refuted (proposal 0037 §6). A.7's two comment blocks (PrimarySuffix `with`, NewExpr) are rewritten to record-only semantics; comments, not productions.
- **The construct-specific disposal window dissolves.** §22.11's unattached-owned rule (instance unbound during the setter sequence, implicit `try`/`finally`) restated §28.3's exception-path discharge for a binding the sugar hid; the bind-first rewrite makes the instance an ordinary owned local from the moment it exists, and §28.3 covers every path with no special text (proposal 0037 §7's per-path trace). The compiler's dedicated landing-pad guard for that window retires with it.
- **Cost history, recorded as the decision's ledger:** the v0.58→v0.59 and v0.69→v0.70 entries were both *reconciliations* of the record/class pun (the first fixed a flatly wrong "`with` does not apply to classes"; the second un-contradicted §9.5 on fresh-record sources); the v0.180 accessibility train had to reconcile two accessibility regimes under one spelling. No recorded decision ever defended the class-source form — a C#-familiarity default, in a language that shipped from the start the named/optional constructor arguments (§22.5) whose absence motivated C#'s feature. What is given up is a spelling — one expression instead of two-to-three statements, or a small factory hoist in nested-expression positions — priced per-position in proposal 0037 §5/§9.
- **Blast radius:** zero uses in the stdlib document, both guides, and all proposals (verified). Conformance corpus: spec_0137 converts to the §9.5 rejection case, spec_0138 (the "Equivalent to" rewrite) deletes with manifest row 140; spec_0288/spec_0293's A.7 embeds drift-absorb at the next A.7 regen. Compiler retirement + test migration (~23 class-source sites across 7 test files) tracked at the issue filed at landing; until it lands, the implemented-but-no-longer-specified window is the established spec-ahead-of-impl pattern (delegated ruling per proposal 0037 Q4).

**`ReadOnlyAsciiByteSpan` retired — five span types, not six (proposal 0038 graduated; tracking #1649).** The sixth and weakest member of the span family — the v0.106 read-only byte view over an ASCII string, with its construction surface `string.AsAsciiByteSpan()` / `TryAsAsciiByteSpan(out)` — is deleted. This is a **changed-circumstances retirement** of the recorded v0.106 decision, not a re-litigation of it as decided: the FFI half of the v0.106 motivation never materialized (records are categorically not FFI-compatible, spec §32.5; the actual boundary carriers for string bytes are `CString`/`RawBytes`, stdlib §10, allocating-copying by design), and the I/O half was overtaken in normative text by v0.165's span-destination encoding (#1355): `Encoding.GetByteCount(s)` + `GetBytes(s, destination: Span<byte>)` encodes into a caller-reused `OwningBuffer<byte>` with zero per-call allocation, for **every** string, with no conditional-on-storage caveat — whereas the retired view's own zero-copy claim was conditional from birth (§3.4's per-access-cost paragraph: implementations are expected to use 1-byte storage for ASCII strings, 'but the language does not require it'). Rulings and edits:

- **Stdlib §3.4 is tombstoned, not renumbered** (delegated ruling per proposal 0038 Q2, matching 0037 Q3's reasoning — §3.3 and the §4.x sections are externally cited and must not shift). The tombstone routes every former use case: one-shot `GetBytes(s)` (allocating, always correct); the span-destination form for allocation-conscious paths; the array's or buffer's own span for `IReadOnlySpan<byte>`-consuming APIs.
- **§9.6 and spec §4.6 teach the two-form `GetBytes` routing** (delegated ruling per Q3): the replacement prose names the v0.165 span-destination form explicitly as the allocation-conscious path — it was previously easy to miss next to the classic allocating `GetBytes(s)` — rather than merely deleting the old advertisement.
- **The re-addition trigger is recorded** (delegated ruling per Q4): rationale §5.15's retirement note records that a future *validated-only* byte view (construction APIs only, no public unchecked constructor) is the sanctioned shape if profiling evidence ever demands one — the door is documented rather than re-argued. Deletion is reversible additively; the shipped hazard and the six-way family tax would not have been.
- **The per-type family tax retires six→five** everywhere a rule walks the span family: stdlib §4.16 (the enumeration, the implements-table row, and the SequenceEqual-through-the-interface example, retargeted to a `ReadOnlySpan<byte>`/`ReadOnlyArraySpan<byte>` pair); spec §28.3's producer-table exclusion row and §28.11's move-exclusion sentence (each list one name shorter, semantics unchanged — no remaining type gains or loses `move`); spec §29.2's dedicated desugaring paragraph (deleted — no other paragraph referenced it); Appendix D.2's Buffers-and-spans row (stdlib §3.3–3.4 → §3.3); and stdlib §1's acronym-naming exemplar pair, which shrinks by deletion — `IeeeEquals` remains the exemplar; the v0.165 #1359 ruling itself is untouched.
- **A documented hazard ceases to exist.** The type's admitted-but-unchecked positional constructor was the standard library's only construction surface documented as silently corrupting data on misuse (§3.4: narrowing a code point above 127 to its low 8 bits, 'an obvious bug' — documented, never fixed). Every retention plan owed a fix; retirement owes nothing.
- **What is genuinely lost, recorded honestly:** the O(1)-setup, allocation-free, borrowed byte view of an ASCII string's own storage. Every replacement performs one O(n) copy into a fresh array or a reused buffer. The loss is narrow (the zero-copy property was implementation-conditional; per-access reads were width-dispatched in the general case) and evidence-free — no such program exists in the corpus, the guides, the proposals, or the test suite.
- **Blast radius:** nothing builds on the type — the one cross-type bridge, `SequenceEqual(other: ReadOnlySpan<byte>)`, was declared on the retired type itself, one-directionally, so its deletion strands no other type's surface; `SequenceEqual` is the stdlib's only `IReadOnlySpan<byte>`-consuming API (verified by exhaustive enumeration). The compiler never implemented the surface (#971 records the family as 'Not started'; item 3 closes as retired — items 1, 2, and 4 remain open and unaffected). Conformance corpus (hand-maintained per #1380): stdlib_0032 deletes with manifest row 358 (already skip/blocked-on-#971); stdlib_0107 trims its two method lines (row 433, skip:signature, stays). Compiler retirement — five name-classification mentions plus one deferral comment, zero functional surface — tracked at the issue filed at landing. Rationale living sections §5.15/§15/§18 adjusted; changelogs are append-only history and retain the v0.106–v0.109 record. Proposals 0009/0029 each drop a one-phrase implementor mention at their next touch. Guides: zero uses (verified).

**Extension specificity pruned to one rule (spec §26.5, §26.5.1; rationale §17.10) — proposal 0039 graduated.** §26.5.1's three-relation specificity ordering is reduced to rule 1 alone — subtype ordering on **receiver-substituted heads** — now stated over *applicable* candidates (extension members of the called name matching the call's arity and argument types, block-level `where` clauses satisfied; a `where` clause is an applicability filter, never a ranking signal). Deleted: rule 2 (recursive more-concrete ordering on declared generic heads — `extension IEnumerable<int>` auto-beating `extension IEnumerable<T>`) and rule 3 (constraint-implication ordering, whose "implied by" was the language's only — and never-specified — constraint-entailment judgment), and with them the v0.183 two-views clarification (rule 1 on substituted heads, rule 2 on declared heads): one relation, one view. Every collision the deleted rules would have ordered is the existing §26.5 rule-4 ambiguity error, whose diagnostic is now normatively required to identify each candidate by defining module, declared head (including its `where` clause), and declaration site — extension blocks are nameless — and whose remedies gain §22.6's distinct-names posture (narrow an import; hoist into a static-class helper; if both blocks are yours, rename one member). The §26.5.1 worked example is retargeted from the deleted rule-2 pair to a rule-1 pair (`extension Array<T>` beats `extension IEnumerable<T>` for an `Array<int>` receiver) plus the same-head ambiguity illustration. Neither deleted rule was ever implemented (#1307: the compiler applies first-declared-wins, silently order-dependent) or exercised (complete stdlib inventory, proposal 0039 §5: every same-name pair across overlapping stdlib extension blocks differs in arity, so applicability alone decides every stdlib call); rule-1-plus-ambiguity therefore reproduces today's stdlib resolution exactly. *Declined:* auto-ranked generic specialization and constraint-implication ranking, with rule 2's re-addition condition recorded (compatible widening — only converts ambiguity errors into resolutions — on demonstrated demand; none for rule 3): rationale §17.10. Migration: none — no document, test, or program depends on the deleted orderings; #1307 is re-scoped to "implement §26.5.1 rule-1 ranking over applicable candidates plus the §26.5 rule-4 candidate-identifying ambiguity diagnostic (replacing first-declared-wins)".

**Owning inline arrays demoted to Extended — the move-only value-type category becomes a new Appendix D.2 feature (proposal 0036 graduated; tracking #1551).** Conformance staging only: no rule changes meaning, no program changes behavior, there is no migration, and the reference compiler (Full-level) is untouched. What changes is what a *Core* conformance claim obligates an implementation to build. Appendix D.2 gains a standalone clause-level row — **Move-only value types (owning inline arrays)** — on the existing FFI-clause/buffer-clause precedent: §15.1.1 and the `owned` slot marker of A.5's `InlineArrayType`; §15.3; §17.13's move-only discard clause; the owning-inline-array field clauses of §28.5 (including the double-marking rejection) and §22.13; §28.7's move-only clause; §28.11's move-only element-category row; §29.2's owned-slot desugaring clauses and §29.8's move-only paragraph; and the §7.10/§14.2 `where T: value` instantiation checks. D.2's closing Core paragraph adds the row's §28 clauses to its exception list, and D.3 records the dependency shape: the feature depends only on Core, and no other Extended feature depends on it — Buffers and spans rejects move-only element types, and Asynchronous programming's two references (§30.14 transfer-closure rule 2's owning-inline-array field alternative; §30.1's move-only-parameter frame clause) are normative only for implementations of both features, the Core→Extended reference rule generalized to Extended→Extended. Why demote: the category's Core status was a **default, never a decision** — Appendix D's v0.132 birth list never considered it, and no changelog through v0.185 records a placement choice; it is the affine model's one surviving carve-out (whole-value reassignment of a move-only array leaks its non-moved-from slots, deferred at #1385 — the exception §28.3/§28.7 name); it is the single place Core value types stop being copy-simple (moved-from state on value-typed locals, fields, and slots; per-slot move tracking and restoration; the instantiation-time copy audit; a third slot category in every storage-position dispatch — a surface whose implementation cost the reference compiler's own §28-family bug history quantifies); it is a leaf — no stdlib type stores, accepts, or returns a move-only value (the stdlib's mentions are exclusions), and records, properties, boxing, sendability, and FFI all reject it; and Core loses no expressiveness — a Core program uses the Core owning collections (`OwningArray<T>` et al.), giving up only the zero-allocation inline form, while rationale §5.14's self-hosting substrate (`OwningBuffer<T>` **plus** `[N owned]T?`) was already half-Extended (Buffers and spans) and now sits whole on one side of the partition, where its story is told at the level — Full — at which it is true. One grammar token gates the whole category: a Core implementation rejects the `owned` marker at the `InlineArrayType` form site with D.1's feature-naming diagnostic, and every downstream rule is unreachable — the cheapest reject-obligation of any D.2 row; the grammar production itself is unchanged. Descriptive tendrils (§3.2's taxonomy note, §8.3's equality row, §8.6's boxing exclusion, §9.7's record exclusion, §17.11's `default()` admission, §23.5's property rejection, §28.1's slot-marker bullet and obligations row, §28.3's carve-out record, §28.8.1, §28.9's capture-as-borrow clause — since v0.184 an instance of §28.3's general captured-owned-bindings rule — §28.10's `using var` clause, §19.3's move-only-scrutinee pattern-binding borrow rule (v0.184, post-dating the proposal; carved-in-effect by the same unreachability reasoning as the capture clause, while its §15.3 statement rides the row's §15.3 listing), §14.4's buffer-side move-only rejection, Appendix C's invariant rows, stdlib §4.14's exclusions, the reflection kind predicates) stay as untagged prose, exactly as the carved FFI/buffer clauses read: under D.1 they are vacuous in a Core implementation. Delegated rulings (owner acceptance 2026-07-12; each resolved per proposal 0036 §10's own recommendation): **Q1** standalone row, not folded into Buffers and spans — neither feature depends on the other, and D.1 diagnostics should name the feature actually tripped; **Q2** the row is named for the §15.3 *category* with its sole inhabitant parenthesized — if user-defined move-only types ever arrive (a door rationale §5.14 leaves open), they land in an existing row; **Q3** carve-out granularity follows the FFI precedent — obligation-bearing clauses in the row, tendrils untagged; **Q4** the capture-clause location was re-verified against the landed v0.184 capture text — the move-only capture-as-borrow clause remains in §28.9 and is deliberately *not* in the row (it is now subsumed by a general Core rule), so the proposal's re-verification condition is discharged; **Q5** sequencing — the demotion lands now, independent of #1385 (move-only whole-value drop-on-overwrite) and #1549 (the §15.3 leak warning §15.3 mandates but the reference compiler does not emit), both of which remain open and recommended: after #1385 the affine claim is carve-out-free at *both* levels, Core by exclusion and Full by fix. Test-suite staging — the partition's stated purpose ("the test-suite and teaching material can follow the same boundary") — is tracked at the retag issue filed at landing.

### v0.189 changelog (v0.188 → v0.189)

**Editorial: history narration removed from normative text; rationale front-matter accuracy (owner review, 2026-07-14).** No rule changes.

- **Spec §2.5.** The circular-imports paragraph opened with a bolded parenthetical narrating the v0.164 defect it replaced, and closed with a note on what "this sentence previously asserted" (v0.181). Both narrations are deleted: the spec's own front matter says it "does not narrate its own history," and this changelog already records both corrections (v0.164, v0.181). The rule text is unchanged.
- **Rationale §1 (The big picture).** The overview claimed "plenty of languages give you any two of these comfortably; Bezel's whole reason for existing is the attempt to hold all three together" — a framing that undersells the field (Rust delivers all three goals) and so misstates what is actually distinctive. Rewritten: the three goals are common ambitions; the defining constraint is holding them with a memory model small enough to learn in full, priced between the borrow checker and the garbage collector.
- **Rationale §3.2 (The discard `_`).** Called the expression-statement discard "the Bezel-specific addition" — false: C# has the discard-assignment `_ = expression;` (C# 7). Rewritten around the true difference: in C# the discard is optional intent-marking atop silent result drops; in Bezel it is the sanctioned opt-out from the spec §21.9 discarded-result warning and (since v0.184) the announced-consume form for named owned bindings.
- **Rationale §3.4 (compound assignment).** Retitled — the never-seriously-considered `+:=` strawman is out of the heading — and compressed to the two decline reasons that matter (no precedent; the evaluate-the-target-once guarantee).
- **Rationale §4.4 (allocation failure).** Now states the termination mechanism up front (report + abort, nothing catchable, no unwinding, no disposal-at-exit — spec §31.4) and answers the C `malloc`-checking instinct directly, instead of opening with the revision number that introduced the rule.

**Migration.** None — documentation-only; no rule changes, no example changes.

### v0.190 changelog (v0.189 → v0.190)

**Defect-fix revision from the 2026-07-14 sweep** — the first full sweep since v0.183, covering the never-swept v0.186–v0.188 seams and the whole spec. 176 findings; every substantive finding adversarially re-verified before landing (21 verified for this revision, 0 refuted); the one critical finding passed a designer→independent-critic gate with all amendments incorporated. The editorial mass (history-narration removal, ~150 sites) lands separately in v0.191.

**Task-family calls produce owned frames — "calls mint, storage lends" (§28.3 new subsection; §28.6, §28.10, §28.12, §30.1, §30.5, Appendix C.3/C.6; stdlib §6.7 note; tracking #1786).** Resolves the sweep's critical contradiction: §28.3's producers table classified a non-`owned` Task-family return from an *instance* method as a borrow of the receiver, while §30's entire disposal story — §30.1's `using var task := client.GetAsync(url);`, §30.5's `AcquireAsync` sketch and disposing-unconsumed example, §30.15's `Receive` — requires those results to be caller-owned fresh tasks; by the letter, every unmarked instance/interface/function-value Task-family call minted a frame nobody owned (and no rule can key on `async`, which is signature-invisible, §28.12). The rule: a call whose *declared* (pre-substitution, nullability-stripped, alias-resolved) return type is `Task`/`Task<T>`/`OwningTask<T>` produces an **owned** task at the call site — no marker, no factory warning (the declared type is the announcement, the iterator-convention parallel); reads of *storage* (property, field, indexer, local) remain borrows. Callee-side the unmarked Task-family return type is container-ownership-transferring: a non-`async` body must return an owned task — fresh frame, forwarded call result, completed-task factory, owned local or `owned` parameter, `move`d owned field, or `null` on a nullable path — and a *stored* task is re-exposed through a property, field, or slot, never a method return (generalizing v0.184's TCS source-owns-task/`.Task`-property decision). Generic bare-type-parameter returns stay unclassified at every instantiation (`First<T>()` at `T = Task<int>` remains a borrow). *Declined:* requiring `owned` on every fresh-task-returning signature (churns every async signature in every program — §30.1's return-type list, C.5, function types, both of this document's §12 decision trees — and silently reintroduces the leak wherever the marker is omitted); post-substitution keying (unsound at `First<T>`). The existing `owned` markers on `Domain.Spawn`/`Parallel.*` become emphasis, not contrast — recorded deliberately against the v0.186 note that the two spellings were "deliberate, not to be silently harmonized": this is the non-silent harmonization that note demanded. The independent critique's amendments are incorporated: the §28.6/C.3 general owned-escape bullets carry explicit Task-family carve-outs (no re-created contradiction pair), the callee-side source enumeration is closed (null arm; owned locals/params), and the frame-return exemption is scoped to carried borrows for Task-family method-or-lambda returns.

**Primitive interface conformance: one type, two sources (§14.2 clause 5 + worked example, §11.8; closes #1696; tracking #1782).** Clause 5's parenthetical ("the wrapper records `Int32` etc. are separate types") contradicted §3.4's one-type alias rule, and the `IComparable<int>` worked example never admitted `int` itself — under that reading the whole comparable surface over primitives failed constraint checking. Resolved for the §3.4 reading: a primitive conforms to (a) the interfaces its stdlib record-syntax declaration lists (`int` → `IComparable<int>`/`IEquatable<int>` — the declaration *is* the primitive's library surface), and (b) the §11.8 compiler-provided set, now stated per stdlib §2.19's actual conformance line: the numeric tower gets all three of `INumber<T>`/`ISteppable<T>`/`IParsable<T>`; `char` gets `ISteppable<char>`/`IParsable<char>` only. Both spec sites had granted `char` an `INumber<T>` conformance the stdlib denies — the stdlib governs its own surface.

**Out-of-range literals are compile errors at formation (§4.2/§4.3; tracking #1781).** Previously a missing rule: §4.2's range rules were scoped to unsuffixed integer literals, and no rule governed `5000000000U` or `1e999`. Ruled: a suffixed integer literal that does not fit its suffix's type, a floating-point literal whose magnitude exceeds its type's largest finite value, and an out-of-range `m`-suffixed decimal literal are compile errors; a float literal otherwise denotes the nearest representable value and never rounds to `±Infinity`. *Declined:* saturating float literals to `±Infinity` — §6.3's overflow-to-Infinity posture explicitly governs *operations*; the recorded literal posture is range-checked-against-the-announced-type, `decimal` has no saturation target (so error is the only rule uniform across the three families), and precedent languages reject.

**Pattern-B consume scoped to plain owned bindings (§30.5, Appendix C.6; tracking #1785).** One sentence claimed a `using var`-bound `OwningTask<T>` is statically consumed by `await`, contradicting the single-consumer paragraph and C.6 (runtime `InvalidOperationException`). Resolved for the majority reading, which §28.3's no-move-out-of-`using var` rule forces: the static consume applies to plain owned locals, `owned` parameters, and drained iteration variables; a `using var` binding's await is the borrowed-operand case (implicit disposal at the await; second await faults at runtime; scope-end dispose is an idempotent no-op).

**Verified defect batch (the rest of the 21).** `scoped` removed from Appendix B.1's unconditionally-reserved list — the B.2 contextual entry (v0.180, #1439) governs (#1783). §7.9's local sentence now states the assigned-before-read regime for locals of defaultless value types instead of claiming every value-typed local "gets the default" (#1784). §15.4's `Set<T>` literal iteration-order claim corrected to stdlib §4.10's insertion-order guarantee (first occurrences in textual order; the "not the literal order" caveat is true only of `OwningSet<T>`'s unordered iteration). §28.9's `Box<T>`/`OwningBox<T>` examples repaired to compile (primary constructors; the field declarations violated §7.9/§7.10 must-initialize). §32.8's registry example gains its required `static owned readonly` and the correct rule-4 suppression-list justification (`Locked<T>` is deliberately not form-(i)). Appendix C's blocking-acquisition list completed with the v0.186 data-owning locks. Plus smaller example, prose-truth, and cross-reference repairs (§11.8's stdlib qualifier; the two `[§7]` citations repointed at §7's actual anchor; §7.11's label corrected to §3.5).

**Migration.** Compile-time, newly **rejected**: `char` (and `bool`/`string`) under `where T: INumber<T>` (#1782); out-of-range suffixed integer, float, and decimal literals (#1781); stored-task borrow returns from non-`async` methods and lambdas — re-expose through a property (#1786); second await of a plain-var owned task (moved-from; was a runtime `InvalidOperationException` by the letter) and an instance task call nested as a plain argument to an escaping Task-family callee — bind first (#1786). Newly **legal**: `scoped` as an ordinary identifier (#1783); `int` under `IComparable<int>`/`IEquatable<int>` routed through its stdlib declaration (#1782); owned task temporaries passed to `owned` parameters (e.g. populating an `OwningArray<OwningTask<T>>` from call results) (#1786). Newly **warned**: a plain-`var` task binding that is only borrow-awaited draws the §28.3 must-use warning (#1786). Behavior change on letter-legal programs: an unbound task temporary consumed only by borrowing uses now disposes — abandons — at end of statement, where the letter previously implied a leak (#1786). Verify-only deltas: #1784 (§7.9 locals), #1785 (second-await split). Doc-only: everything else.

**Editorial and readability revision — the 2026-07-14 sweep's non-semantic mass.** No rule changes; every restructure carries a one-for-one preservation check against the text it replaces.

- **History narration removed from normative text (~150 sites, spec-wide).** The sweep enumerated every instance of the spec narrating its own past — "(v0.NNN — previously …)" parentheticals, "this sentence previously asserted…" notes, superseded-mechanism walkthroughs (§22.8's ordering narrative, §28.7's v0.89–v0.160 archaeology, §30.5's await-binding history, §32.5's "History:" aside, four Appendix A grammar comments) — and reduced each to the current rule plus, where it dates a rule, a bare "(v0.NNN)" pin. The governing principle is recorded durably in `spec-change-process.md` §7; accordingly the spec's opening line about its own history is deleted, with the changelog pointer folded into the companion-documents sentence.

Plus §16.3: the general `Range<T>` operations (`IsOpenEnded`, `IsEmpty`, the `Contains` formula, `GetEnumerator`) relocated out of the `Range<char>` iteration subsection under a new "Range operations" heading at their long-standing anchor.

- **Rationale accuracy batch (25 fact-check findings; 4 sections rewritten).** The prose body was fact-checked claim-by-claim (210 links verified; every other-language statement audited). Corrected: §2.1's C# `internal` description (assembly-scoped — "internal to a namespace" is not a C# concept; the paragraph now states C#'s actual lexical-lookup behavior and why it trains the wrong intuition); §6.1's smart-cast attribution (TypeScript, not Kotlin — Kotlin refuses to narrow mutable properties precisely to avoid the TOCTOU this section warns about); §16.1's Python ctypes description (a hand-declared FFI, Bezel's own approach; the header-driven generators are bindgen/ctypesgen/SWIG); §5.16's `Array<byte>.NewBuffer` (an API that does not exist) replaced with the real surface; §9.5's `sealed` description aligned with spec §12.4 (plain `sealed` forbids all inheritance; module-boundary sealing is the `sealed abstract` combination); §5.15's C# Span-in-async claim updated for C# 13; the blanket "records are not FFI-compatible" narrowed to the v0.186 truth (§32.13 C-compatible records exist; *spans* are borrow-carrying and stay out) at both rationale sites and the stdlib §3.4 echo; two "static interface members are deferred" passages updated (shipped v0.176); the misplaced `sec-ffi` anchor relocated to §16's heading; stale issue-status parentheticals refreshed. Rewritten outright: **§5.11** (its `OwningCache<T>` example was spec-invalid post-v0.169 — it now matches spec §14.4's marker-corrected form and the narration explains the current semantics: destructor cascade, call-site transfer marker, the iterator-factory return convention); **§5.9** (the v0.61 informational warning it presented as the standing design was dropped in v0.66 — now describes trivial-dispose as the §3.6 derived property it is); **§20 Closing** (the pre-compiler-era "what remains is implementation" replaced with the current mode: a working reference compiler exercised by a spec-derived suite, with the spec normative and divergences tracked as issues).
