Newly-declared surface that was already normative by prose: `Counter<K>`'s `IEnumerable<DictionaryEntry<K, int>>` conformance clause (stdlib §4.20) and the four temporal `ToString` declarations (stdlib §2.5) — conforming implementations already provide these, so no program changes meaning. Guide 2's and Guide 3's revalidation pins move to v0.227 (Guide 3's examples were re-traced in full and carry no text changes); Guide 1 keeps its v0.223 pin — this sweep verified its v0.223-train mirrors and spot-checked the remainder, short of the full re-trace a pin bump asserts.

### v0.228 changelog (v0.227 → v0.228)

**Design change — small-stdlib ergonomics batch II (proposal 0067 graduates; owner-accepted 2026-07-28).** Five symmetry completions land in the standard library, each the missing member of a pair the library had already opened; no spec change, no new types, no grammar change. The proposal's five open questions are resolved at this landing, recorded per item below.

- **Span-source encode (stdlib §3.2).** `Encoding` gains `GetByteCount(s: ReadOnlyStringSpan)`, `GetBytes(s: ReadOnlyStringSpan, destination: Span<byte>)`, and the one-shot `GetBytes(s: ReadOnlyStringSpan): owned Array<byte>` — the input-side mirror of the v0.222 span-source decode, reaching the allocation-conscious encode path from a span without materializing the intermediate string. Identical contract to the string forms over the span's code-point range; strict fault model unchanged; `ReadOnlyStringSpan` is not borrow-bearing, so no lifetime restriction rides the parameter. **Q1 resolved:** the members are `abstract` — the no-external-users premise is confirmed at this landing; the silently-allocating `virtual`-default alternative stays declined (it would hide the allocation from exactly the callers who chose the span path for allocation reasons).
- **`Math` decimal symmetry (stdlib §2.2).** `Sign(decimal): int` and `Floor`/`Ceiling`/`Truncate(decimal): decimal` join their `double` siblings beside the existing `Abs(decimal)`; all exact, never faulting (`decimal`'s range endpoints are integral). **Declined** (carried from the proposal): a static `Math.Round(decimal, digits)` — the instance `Decimal.Round(digits)` (§9.3) already carries the pinned banker's-rounding contract, and a static twin would be two names for one operation. Note the overload-resolution edge these three members introduce for integer arguments (see Migration); adding exact-match integer overloads to absorb it was declined — `Floor`/`Ceiling`/`Truncate` of an already-integral value is a no-op that usually marks a latent bug (`Ceiling` over an integer division has already truncated), and the loud §22.6 ambiguity error names the mistake.
- **Radix `TryParse` (stdlib §9.1).** `TryParse(s: string, radix: int, out result: T): bool` (shape (c)) joins the existing `Parse(s, radix)` on the integer types via §9.1's analogous-shapes rule — the previously sole `Parse` in the document without a `Try` twin. False (out = 0) exactly where `Parse` raises `FormatException`/`OverflowException`. **Pin (Q5):** an invalid radix (outside {2, 8, 10, 16}) is a caller bug, not input failure — `ArgumentException` from `Parse` and `TryParse` alike. **Q2 resolved:** the span radix forms stay deferred (recorded in the proposal for a later sweep).
- **`Array<T>` occurrence search (stdlib §4.4).** `IndexOf(item, startIndex)` (bounds `0 <= startIndex <= Count`; `= Count` legal, returns -1 — the v0.215 string-contract mirror) and `LastIndexOf(item)`; equality is `Equals` for both, as the one-argument form; plain `method`, not `pure` (user equality runs). **Declined** (carried): `LastIndexOf(item, startIndex)` (no backward-from-index precedent anywhere, no workload) and a predicate overload (LINQ's axis, proposal 0026). **Q3 resolved:** `OwningArray<T>` parity waits for a workload on the owning type; the proposal records the seam.
- **`TimeSpan` completion (stdlib §2.5).** The anchors `Zero`/`MinValue`/`MaxValue` (static readonly, the `DateTime` precedent), the scalar `operator /(a: TimeSpan, divisor: double)`, and unary `operator -(t: TimeSpan)` complete the operator group `*` opened. Faults: `/` raises `DivideByZeroException` on `divisor = 0.0`; unary `-` of `MinValue` raises `OverflowException`. **Pin (Q5):** the existing `operator *`'s previously-unstated range behavior is pinned with the same rule the new members carry — `OverflowException` on a product/quotient outside the tick range or a NaN operand (`TimeSpan` has no `Infinity`/`NaN`, so the §6.4-style defined-fault stance applies, not §6.3's produce-infinity stance). **Q4 resolved:** the duration-ratio `operator /(a: TimeSpan, b: TimeSpan): double` is not admitted — a second capability the confirmed workloads did not name; recorded liftable in the proposal.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** no ownership rules touched — every addition is value-in/value-out, a borrow-taking query parameter, a call-bounded span borrow, or a fresh owned-array production under §1's existing convention. No kernel rule engaged; axiom register unchanged (twelve live, two tombstones).

**Migration.** Additive, with one resolution edge and two **newly-defined** contract pins. Newly **rejected**: a `Math.Floor`/`Ceiling`/`Truncate` call whose argument is an integer type or `char` — previously legal via the sole `double` overload's implicit conversion, now ambiguous under §22.6's equal-ranking rule (the `double` and `decimal` candidates tie); the remedy is an explicit conversion (`Math.Floor(double(n))`) — or reconsidering the call, since floor/ceiling of an already-integral value is a no-op (`Abs`/`Sign` are unaffected: their `int` overloads give exact matches). The three new `abstract` `Encoding` members make a previously-complete user `Encoding` subclass incomplete — accepted under Q1's confirmed no-external-users premise, the v0.222 span-overloads precedent. The pins state previously-unstated behavior (invalid-radix `ArgumentException` on the existing `Parse(s, radix)`; `TimeSpan.operator *`'s over-Ticks-in-double computation model and range/NaN `OverflowException`) per the v0.215 pin precedent. Everything else is purely additive; the conformance corpus carries no flips (the §9.1 `Int32` signature mirror `stdlib_0101` is skip-listed and lags by design). Proposal 0067 flips to superseded; the implementation tracker is [#2242](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2242). The spec and rationale texts are unchanged this revision — their companion headers move in lockstep — and the guides are untouched (their re-validation pins, v0.223/v0.227/v0.227, stand; a pin is a re-trace assertion, not a companion header).

### v0.229 changelog (v0.228 → v0.229)

**Ruling — the error-model doctrine (proposal 0076's rulings R1–R6, owner-ruled 2026-07-29, accepted as recommended; 0076 flips to superseded).** The Result-vs-exceptions question is answered for Bezel by doctrine, not migration: the failure-signal rule and the error-payload governance rule land as normative stdlib §1 conventions, `SerializationException` gains its typed fault-location surface, and the remaining rulings are recorded dispositions. Nothing is re-classified retroactively; no landed API changes mechanism at this revision.

- **R1 — the failure-signal rule (stdlib §1, new normative convention; cross-referenced from spec §22.16; Guide 2 §6 aligned).** Every fault condition a library surface declares is classified by a five-band first-match procedure — caller bug (`requires`/the residual defect exceptions), expected absence (the value shapes), expected-informative-branch-consumed with a value-like payload (`choice` return), boundary-consumed fault (typed exception, producer-local per spec §31.4), fatal (termination) — one primary mechanism per condition, conditions on one member classifying separately. The band-3/band-4 boundary is fixed as *consumption locus plus payload shape*, never information content: an expected, information-bearing, branch-consumed condition whose payload cannot be value-like (spec §35.4/§35.5/§35.12) takes the typed exception with its reason recorded beside the surface, keeping the classification revisitable. One carve: give-back conditions — a failure path that must hand an owned value back to the caller, stdlib §6.9's send family — are ownership-protocol designs, neither band's material. The no-dual rule closes the procedure: recorded tiers serving different call-site stances (the §9.1 `Parse`/`TryParse` model) are sanctioned; two peer spellings of one stance are a violation the newer spelling loses. **Declined with it:** information content as the band test (it would evacuate the environmental band the §31.1 copy-out model serves); any retroactive re-classification (the rule applied to the v0.228 corpus moves almost nothing — the misfits it flags stand where they are as recorded misfits pending their own rulings: `Console.ReadKey`'s exception-spelled EOF condition, band-2-shaped, its `ReadKeyOrNull` value tier queued with proposal 0072's graduation; the §2.5 `Add*` blame relabel, deferred on the graduation-checklist tracker [#2338](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2338); the defect and fatal bands are untouched, and the environmental band stays put with recorded reasons). Spec §22.16's boundary paragraph gains the one-sentence pointer to the rule; Guide 2 §6 aligns (the `choice` row gains the branch-consumption and value-payload conjuncts its old wording lacked, the table gains the boundary-consumed-fault row, and the band-3/4 boundary and catch-at-boundary sentences land as prose; revalidation pin moves to v0.229). The rule is written against landed classification facts only — the open async-container question stays where it is filed ([#2255](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2255)) and is asserted nowhere as a rule.
- **R4 — error-payload governance (stdlib §1, beside the rule).** Error-payload types live with their producer — declared alongside it, carrying its import — the spec §31.4 producer-locality discipline transposed from the exception taxonomy to `Result`/domain-choice error payloads; value-like unless a recorded ruling states otherwise; one producer family, one payload type (a second module extends by wrapping, never by widening); case-set growth on a shipped payload type is gated by recorded ruling exactly as exception-taxonomy growth is. **Why with R1:** choices are closed sums — every case addition breaks every exhaustive consumer (spec §35.6) — so an ungoverned payload vocabulary would fragment faster than the exception hierarchy the §31.4 discipline keeps meaningful; adoption without governance was declined for exactly that reason.
- **R3(a) — `SerializationException`'s typed surface (stdlib §2.15, §2.17).** The class shape is declared at its producer's home: `Offset: long?` (byte offset of the fault, binary; `null` for JSON) and `Line: int?`/`Column: int?` (JSON; `null` for binary) — value-typed, copy-out-friendly under spec §31.1's snapshot model, on the `ArgumentException.ParamName` precedent for exception types carrying typed value surface. **Newly-defined pin landed with it:** all three properties are `null` on a write-side raise (the JSON non-finite-float rule), where there is no input to locate. §2.15's prose now points at the declared properties instead of asserting surface no declaration carried. **Sequenced, not declined:** R3's second half — a `Result` dual with a value-like `SerializationError` payload at proposal 0073's recorded `TryParse<T>` seam — waits for the decode-cluster pilot under R2's scope; the typed-surface fix serves every existing consumer under the band-4 copy-out model first, and the throwing form remains the assert-shaped tier throughout. **[#2276](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2276) fixed in the same stroke:** stdlib §2.17's "one built-in carries surface" counting sentence now enumerates by reference (`ArgumentException` — spec §31.4, `TypeInitializationException`, `SerializationException` — §2.15), and spec §31.4's parallel "the one built-in" phrasing is de-counted (`ArgumentException.ParamName` is declared in the same section). #2276 closes at this landing.
- **R2/R5/R6 — dispositions recorded, no further normative edit at this revision.** **R2 (adoption scope): the hybrid is accepted** — `Result` adoption confined to the decode/deserialize and gathered-value-error clusters, value-like payloads only, riding proposal 0075's stages 1–2 under R4's governance. It is enacted by the rule plus later per-surface graduations, each its own owner-gated tier ruling; nothing migrates wholesale, and maximal Result stays recorded as not currently constructible, reopenable only at 0076 §6's four-condition bar. **R5 (propagation operator): stays gated** — 0061 §2's evidence gate as re-armed by 0075 §4.2 (observed per-call ceremony in code written *with* stages 1–2, never predicted ceremony), and the four-way `?` token collision means an activated gate opens onto a spelling design, not a rubber stamp. **R6 (frontier wording): at their graduations,** proposals 0007 and 0011 reword their taxonomy justifications from "the errors-are-typed-values discipline of Guide 2 §5" to the ground the rule now supplies — an expected environmental condition consumed at boundaries is a distinct catchable type, producer-local per spec §31.4, band 4 of the failure-signal rule — a graduation-checklist obligation recorded here and tracked as [#2338](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2338) (0012's Try-dual re-scope to the absence axis is flagged on the same tracker for its own graduation).

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** no ownership rules touched — the rulings are doctrine (a classification procedure and a governance rule) plus additive exception surface; the rule *cites* the §35.4 classification and §35.5 owning-match machinery and engages none of it. No kernel rule added or lifted; axiom register unchanged (twelve live, two tombstones).

**Migration.** Doc-only plus newly-declared additive surface. No program changes meaning; no grammar production, anchor, or section number moves; the conformance corpus carries no flips. The failure-signal and governance rules re-classify almost nothing landed — they bind new and re-ruled fault declarations and the recorded-tier process, and the flagged misfits (`Console.ReadKey`'s EOF spelling, the §2.5 `Add*` blame labels) stand as recorded misfits until their own rulings. Newly-declared surface that was previously prose-only: `SerializationException.Offset`/`Line`/`Column` (stdlib §2.15), with the write-side-null pin newly defined — spec-ahead-of-impl, implementation tracker [#2337](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2337) filed at this landing. Guide 2's revalidation pin moves to v0.229 (its §5 examples re-trace cleanly under the rule: `ParsePort` is band 3, `TryTakeCached` band 2); Guide 3's §3 failure-signal sentence re-words to the rule's test and its pin moves to v0.229 with Guide 2's; Guide 1 is untouched and keeps its pin. Proposal 0076 flips to superseded and the README queue row moves with it; #2276 closes; the study's open spec seams (#2255, #2256, #2257) remain open and are deliberately untouched — band 4's residual clause is written against the landed §35.4/§35.12 facts alone. The rationale gains §11.4, giving the doctrine's declines a citable home — why information content is not the band test, and why maximal `Result` is recorded as not currently constructible, with the reopening bar; its companion header moves in lockstep.

### v0.230 changelog (v0.229 → v0.230)

**Spec-rulings batch — eleven owner-ruled issues (2026-07-29; owner-directed landing).** Underspecified and contradictory cases across the async/ownership seam, the pure fragment, statement totality, `ref`/`out` locations, statics, and the stdlib's IO/format/search/LINQ surfaces — each landing the owner's recorded ruling with the decision, the declined alternatives, and the reasons.

**Move-only value task results rejected (#2255, §30.5 + §30.4 + §35.4 — soundness).** §30.5's producer taxonomy names the missing case: a move-only value result type (an owning-classified choice instantiation, §35.4 rule 1, or an owning inline array, §15.1.1) is admitted by **no** row — `Task<T>`/`OwningTask<T>` over such a T is a compile error at the declaration, because §30.4's multi-award rule would hand the same must-move-exactly-once value to every awaiter (and `OwningTask<T>` admits class T only). The copyable-value rows are re-spelled "copyable value type" so the taxonomy composes; §35.4's owning-choice paragraph gains the completing async sentence its borrow-bearing neighbor already carried. **Declined:** a single-award container admission for move-only value results — real design work (the error-model study's ▲H2), its own proposal if wanted, never a patch row here. Impl delta: the async-return admission checks head names only, so `Task<Result<C,E>>` is silently admitted at HEAD (#2255 tracks).

**Pure fragment × choices closed both ways (#2256, §22.15).** Rule 3's closed construction list gains **choice construction** (§35.3's payload-free reference and payload-case application), provided every payload argument is itself pure-admissible — mirroring record construction's proviso; an `owned` payload slot stays an owned-consuming position, so an owning-classified construction remains unwritable in a pure body. The return restriction extends in step: alongside the `owned` class-typed return, a **move-only value return** (owning choice, owning inline array) is rejected — same deferred-error reason, same remedy. **Declined:** the not-named-so-rejected reading of rule 3 — it would contradict §22.16's prover fragment (which already names choice-case analysis) and make `Result` unusable in the pure fragment the verification strategy leans on. Impl delta tracked (#2256).

**Compound-statement totality is ordinary reachability (#2257, §21.7 — clarification).** Compound statements (`if`/`elif`/`else`, `try`/`catch`/`finally`) satisfy the every-exit-path rule by ordinary reachability over their completion edges; the statement-`case` bullet remains the sole exhaustiveness-keyed grant. Doc-only; the implementation already reads it exactly this way (`stmtAlwaysExits`).

**Block-form static properties are admitted `ref`/`out` targets (#2322, §22.3 — interpretation 1).** The mutable-static exclusion's subject is re-spelled to match §22.12 rule 2's own — "no mutable static **field or auto-property**" — and one sentence names the block-form (accessor-bodied) static property an admitted property target under the existing copy-in/copy-out bracket: the exclusion's stated reason (store semantics defined for direct assignment only) is about raw field storage, which a computed property does not have — its setter body performs exactly the direct assignment the exclusion preserves. **Declined:** excluding all settable statics (simplest to state; costs an admitted §22.3 category for no stated reason). Impl delta: both spellings are rejected at HEAD by the #1302 bracket's deliberate static decline (#2322 tracks).

**The `ref`/`out` exact-type rule stated where it binds (#2282, §22.3 + §14.5).** §22.3's ref/out-locations subsection gains the general rule: the argument's static type must be exactly the parameter's referent type — no §5.1 implicit conversion, not even a widening one an ordinary by-value argument would take at the §22.6 applicability check. §14.5's exact-unification bullet gains the §22.3 cross-reference and reads as the general rule's inference-time instance rather than its sole statement. Doc-only: the compiler already enforces exactly this (#1756/#2266); the diagnostic's §14.5-outside-its-scope citation can simplify to §22.3.

**Generic-parameter-typed mutable statics rejected at the declaration (#2331, §22.12 rule 2 — option 1).** One sentence makes the rejection explicit: a mutable static field or auto-property whose declared type is a bare generic parameter or its nullable form matches no admitted form and is a compile error at the declaration site, whatever the constraints or eventual substitutions — generic classes' statics, statics of types nested in generic types, and generic methods' statics alike. Why: rule 2's admission is keyed to the declared type alone so the check stays decidable at the declaration (form (ii) states the principle); per-monomorphization checking (interpretation 2) would make admission a property of the instantiation set, and a bound-keyed admission (interpretation 4) rarely pins the category. **Declined:** per-monomorphization checking, bound-keyed admission, and the status quo (silent admission of process-global mutable storage of unbounded category — the hole rule 2 exists to close). Impl delta: HEAD admits the shape (the #1393 rejection was backed out in `adff878` pending this ruling); the two `generic_static_state_536` round-trip pins flip to rejection tests (#2331 tracks).

**`FileStream` constructor contract (#2285 + #2286 rider, stdlib §7.2).** The two-argument constructor implies **`FileAccess.ReadWrite`** — every mode but `Open` creates or rewrites, so a read-only default would strand five of the six modes through the short form (the #645 in-tree reading, now normative). Failed construction raises the §7.5 types: `FileNotFoundException` (missing file under `FileMode.Open`), `DirectoryNotFoundException` (missing directory component), `IOException` otherwise. **Declined:** the mode-dependent .NET access rule (`Append`→`Write` — a second rule for no stated need) and the conservative `Read` default. Impl delta: the shipped §7 runtime returns status codes and a degenerate handle, raising nothing (#2286 is the runtime→exception bridge tracker).

**Empty-needle conventions pinned (#2316, stdlib §3.3 + §9.6).** The mirror is confirmed and stated: `IndexOf` of an empty needle returns `0` (from-index form: the start index, already pinned in §9.6); `Contains`/`StartsWith`/`EndsWith` of an empty needle return `true`; `SequenceEqual` against an empty operand is `true` iff the receiver is empty; a zero-length receiver reads nothing and finds nothing except the empty needle. §9.6 gains the pins it lacked (`Contains("")`/`StartsWith("")`/`EndsWith("")`) beside its existing v0.195/v0.215 comments; §3.3 states the full set in prose. The implementation already behaves this way on both surfaces.

**`IGrouping` single-consumption re-scoped to the outer sequence (#2292, stdlib §5 — reading (b)).** Single-consumption (spec §29.11) binds to the outer lazy `IEnumerable<IGrouping<TKey, T>>` only; a materialized group is an ordinary re-enumerable collection whose elements are the grouping's own buffer, and repeated terminals on one group are defined. The `ToArray` example stays as advice. **Declined:** reading (a), enforcing per-group affinity — §29.11's stated rationale (the borrow lifetime of the query's *source*) does not apply to a buffer the grouping owns outright; enforcement would demand new provenance tracking with per-outer-iteration reset and would flip the shipped five-terminals pin from correct to error. The post-#755 implementation is already correct under (b).

**Decimal format midpoints round half-to-even (#2253, stdlib §2.18).** One midpoint rule: `F`/`P`/`E` over `decimal` round midpoints to banker's, matching §9.3's `Decimal.Round` — two spellings of one rounding operation agree. **Declined:** confining banker's to `Decimal.Round` and keeping the specifiers half-up — it leaves `F` and `P` disagreeing on the same number ×100, and the specifier surface with no stated midpoint rule at all. Impl delta: `F` is banker's at HEAD (via `bz_decimal_round`), `P`/`E` remain hand-rolled half-up (#2253 tracks; the adjacent `Round(digits)` range-contract violation is a separate pre-existing defect, tracked independently).

**Temporal patterns pass through non-specifier characters (#2243, stdlib §2.18 — interpretation (a); proposal 0074 item 4, landing ahead of its batch).** Every character that does not begin a specifier is a literal, copied through verbatim — alphabetic included (`T`, `Z`); the unrecognized-specifier fault governs malformed runs of the specifier letters, not literals. The growth rider lands beside it: the temporal vocabulary grows only by recorded ruling and never by reinterpreting a character that passes through today. **Declined:** quoting/escaping (reserves the letter space at the cost of an escape mechanism §2.18 lacks, and breaks the presupposed unquoted spellings — §2.5's own default rendering and 0010's owner-ruled wire form) and the ad-hoc `T`/`Z` allowlist. 0074's remaining items are unaffected and await their own graduation. Impl delta: the runtime passes non-specifiers through but also passes malformed specifier runs (e.g. `yyy`) as literals where the pinned rule faults (#2243 tracks).

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** the one §30.5-touching ruling (#2255, with #2256's return-restriction echo) is a **derivation** — K1's exactly-one-owner state-match against A3's two-container design (a move-only value satisfies neither container's contract: `Task`'s rows promise no obligation crosses the await and §30.4 multi-awards; `OwningTask` requires class T); no row added, no axiom spent, a missing rejection named. Everything else is control-flow clarification, lvalue-category scoping, statics admission, and stdlib surface. Axiom register unchanged.

**Migration.** Newly **rejected**: `Task<T>`/`OwningTask<T>` declared over a move-only value T (#2255 — silently admitted at HEAD; soundness); a pure member declaring a move-only value return (#2256); mutable statics of bare-generic-parameter type — **restated**: the v0.221 migration note already listed the category among #1393's residual rejections, now explicit rule text, and the standing `generic_static_state_536` round-trip pins flip (#2331). Newly **defined**: `FileStream(path, mode)` ≡ `FileAccess.ReadWrite` plus the §7.5 construction-failure mapping (#2285/#2286); the §3.3/§9.6 empty-needle and empty-receiver conventions (#2316); decimal `F`/`P`/`E` midpoints as half-to-even (#2253 — `P`/`E` outputs change at exact midpoints when enforcement lands); temporal-pattern literal pass-through with the growth rider (#2243 — malformed specifier runs fault once enforced, currently passed through). Newly **accepted**: choice construction in pure bodies (#2256); block-form static properties as `ref`/`out` targets (#2322 — rejected at HEAD by the bracket's decline); repeated terminals on one materialized `IGrouping<TKey, T>` (#2292 — the prior per-group single-consumption sentence made a second terminal a §29.11 violation; the shipped compiler already admitted it). Doc-only / behavior-unchanged: #2257, #2282, and #2316's existing-behavior pins. The conformance corpus carries no example flips (no newly-rejected shape is a committed case; verified by grep at landing); guide revalidation not needed — the guides' `new FileStream(path, mode)` uses gain defined semantics, no idiom retires. Spec-ahead-of-impl deltas are tracked by the issues kept open per ruling: #2255, #2256, #2322, #2331, #2286, #2253, #2243.

### v0.231 changelog (v0.230 → v0.231)

**Design change — the nullable-return convenience tier (proposal 0072 graduates; owner-accepted 2026-07-29).** The `*OrNull` tier gets its recorded rule and its two hottest surfaces: `ParseOrNull` beside every concrete `Parse`/`TryParse` family, `GetOrNull` on the dictionary family, and the §1 taxonomy sentence naming the three access tiers. No spec change, no new types, no grammar change; every Try member keeps its signature, its contract, and (for `TryParse`) its §2.19 constraint-witness role — duals, not conversions: the terminated #1535 fork (v0.222) is engaged, not reopened. The proposal's four open questions are resolved at this landing:

- **`ParseOrNull(s: string): T?` (stdlib §9.1–§9.5, §2.5, §2.6) — Q1 resolved as scoped.** Declared on the seventeen concrete Parse-bearing types (the eight §9.1 integers via the analogous-shapes rule, `double`/`float`, `decimal`, `bool`, `char`, `DateTime`/`DateOnly`/`TimeOnly`, `Guid`): `null` exactly where the type's own `Parse(s)` raises (the `FormatException`/`OverflowException` contract), the parsed value otherwise — one grammar per type, three access forms, no new parsing behavior anywhere. Purity mirrors each type's own `Parse`: `pure` on the §9 primitives, plain `static method` on the temporals and `Guid`; unlike `TryParse` the member declares no out, so it can be pure where its `Parse` is (spec §22.15, the rule recorded at §2.2's `DivRem`). **Declined** (carried from the proposal): the radix and span duals — 19 further members of surface completeness for no capability; those are specialist surfaces whose callers are already in ceremony-tolerant territory, while the tier's whole value is the casual call site holding a `string`. `IParsable<T>` (§2.19) is untouched — the new members are per-type, not constraint surface (the v0.222 span-parse precedent), and the constraint-witnessing `TryParse` members are load-bearing and stay.
- **`GetOrNull(key: K): V?` (stdlib §4.8, §4.17, §4.9) — Q2 resolved: all three types.** Absent → `null`; present → the value under each family's read semantics — a copy for value-typed `V` and `string`, a borrow of the stored value (source: the receiver) for class-typed `V`; at §4.9 always a borrow in the indexer's get posture — a look, not a take (`PopValue`/`TryPopValue` remain the take forms). Not `pure` (key lookup runs user `Equals`/`GetHashCode`/comparers, or `CompareTo` at §4.17 — the v0.215 rule that keeps the `Contains` family impure). The §5 conflation caveat is carried onto §4.8/§4.17 with the four word-substitutions the surface forces (element→value, empty→absent, `Count`→`ContainsKey`, `*OrNull`→`GetOrNull`); §4.9 is criterion-clean — `where V: class` makes the payload statically non-nullable at every instantiation (spec §7.10), so `null` means absent unambiguously and no caveat arises there. The criterion tension was ruled as disclosed: the v0.184/#1535 criterion's letter routes generic-payload lookup to the Try shape; the owner admits the member on the recorded-practice line (§5's `*OrNull` family, v0.215's `Environment.GetInt`/`GetBool`, the 0001/0019 draft `Get`s), caveated — the convenience tier is additive to, never a replacement of, the distinguishing form (`TryGetValue` keeps its shape and role). The spec §7.7 `??` limit at class-typed `V` is recorded beside the §4.8 member: a borrowed result does not meet an owned fallback (borrowed fallbacks compose; fresh fallbacks bind-then-test); the direct `??` composition is the value-typed and `string` sweet spot the member was built for.
- **The §1 tier sentence — Q3 and Q4 resolved.** The Try-convention bullet now names the three access tiers — **throwing** (`Parse`, the `[key]` indexer: absence is a bug), **`*OrNull`** (returns `T?` for direct `??`/`?.` composition where the payload can carry the signal — band 2's nullable-return value shape, a recorded tier in the no-dual rule's sense), and **`Try`** (the only shape that distinguishes the outcomes a collapsed `T?` cannot, spec §7.10) — with shape (b)'s `TryX` spelling staying reserved for acquisition-shaped members whose payload is statically non-nullable. **Naming (Q3): `ParseOrNull`/`GetOrNull`** — the suffix joins the one convention §5 already declares normatively and states the contract in the name. **Declined:** bare `Get` (beside the throwing indexer, `d.Get(k)` hides the KeyNotFoundException-vs-null difference in a name that does not state it; the bare-`Get` precedents outside this batch are protocol-shaped drafts, and §2.4's own `Get` — landed below — is the *sole-accessor* case, no throwing tier beside it, so its name has nothing to distinguish) and Try-prefixed nullable overloads (`TryParse(s): T?` beside `TryParse(s, out): bool` would put shapes (b) and (c) on one member name — the mirror of the one-method-convention problem the #1535 ruling declined). **Q4:** the sentence lands with the members, as the taxonomy repair, not an optional gloss.
- **`Console.ReadKeyOrNull(): char?` (stdlib §2.1) — the v0.229 recorded misfit resolved.** The failure-signal rule's landing flagged `ReadKey`'s exception-spelled EOF condition as band-2-shaped with no value tier, its resolution queued with this graduation (v0.229 entry). The `*OrNull` tier supplies it: `null` at end of input, the key otherwise — `char?` is exactly the `ReadLine` null-at-EOF analog the v0.195 note said was missing, since `char` is a non-nullable value type. `ReadKey` keeps its `EndOfStreamException` contract as the assert-shaped throwing tier; §2.1's recorded no-analog reason is retired.

**Design change — small-stdlib ergonomics batch III (proposal 0074 graduates; owner-accepted 2026-07-29; item 4 landed ahead at v0.230).** One rename (breaking, the batch's only non-additive item), one symmetry addition, one contract pin, one convention sentence, and one disambiguating clause riding the rename; the proposal's §7 considered-and-declined register stands as recorded. Item 4 — the §2.18 temporal pattern-literal pass-through rule and its growth rider — landed at v0.230 with the #2243 ruling and is not re-landed here. The remaining open questions are resolved per item:

- **`Environment.Get`/`Set`/`Variables` (stdlib §2.4) — BREAKING; Q1 and Q2 resolved as recommended.** `GetEnvironmentVariable` → `Get`, `SetEnvironmentVariable` → `Set`, `GetEnvironmentVariables` → `Variables`; every contract unchanged (null-when-absent; null-removes with the v0.195 empty-name/`"="` `ArgumentException` pin; the §1 fresh-instance `owned Dictionary<string, string>` return). The family now has one register: `Get` is the raw `string?` read, `GetInt`/`GetBool` the v0.215 typed conveniences over it. §4.8's no-`Set`-method sentence gains the disambiguating clause (a collections-write-surface rule, not a rule about the name — `Environment.Set` is unrelated). **Declined:** keeping the long names as a rationale-§15.x-style familiarity cost — the §1 v0.165 naming rule governs the casing of names the library *keeps*, not renaming by recorded decision (the v0.168 owning-enumeration family rename is the precedent), and the no-users window closes with the first external user; `GetAll` for the enumeration (a `Get*` name with nothing after "All" to type it) also declined.
- **`String.IsEmpty` (stdlib §9.6) — the symmetry addition.** `public pure readonly property IsEmpty: bool` = (`Length = 0`), O(1) — §3.3's `IsEmpty` spelling restated in `String`'s own declaration style, beside `Length`/`IsAscii`. `IsNullOrEmpty` stays: the static is the null-tolerant form, the property requires a non-null receiver. The boundary stands as recorded: the §4 add/remove collections carry `Count` only and gain no `IsEmpty`; the property belongs to the extent-bearing (`Length`) types, and `String` was the one that lacked it.
- **`Guid.NewGuid` (stdlib §2.6) — the contract pin; Q3 resolved.** A version-4 (random) UUID: version and variant bits fixed (0100 / 10), the remaining 122 bits drawn from the runtime's entropy source (the §1 v0.204 replay-intercept point already declared for §2.6); uniqueness probabilistic, not checked — no dedup, no cross-process coordination. The entropy source is deliberately NOT specified as cryptographically strong — §2.7's recorded posture (cryptographic randomness belongs to the future `System.Security.Cryptography` module; proposal 0068's `RandomNumberGenerator` is that surface) — so `NewGuid` values must not serve as secrets. The pin makes the behavior `CompareTo`'s pinned byte order already made observable (v4 ids sort randomly; a time-ordered generator would sort by creation) defined rather than implementation-chosen. A v7-style time-ordered id stays a capability question recorded in the proposal: if wanted, it arrives as a separately named member by its own proposal, never as a silent version change under the name this pin fixes.
- **The §1 `Count`-vs-`Length` sentence — Q5 resolved: as drafted, closing clause included.** `Length` measures a fixed or contiguous extent (text, buffers and spans, `FrozenArray<T>`, `Stream`, the §10 FFI carriers); `Count` counts membership that grows and shrinks (the `Add`/`Remove`/`Push`/`Enqueue` families); a type declares one or the other, never both — with the resizable-`Array<T>`-vs-.NET clause kept as the arriving reader's anchor.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** no ownership rules touched — the additions are value-in/value-out statics over value types and `string` (`ParseOrNull`, `ReadKeyOrNull`) plus one `pure` instance property on the runtime-managed `String` (`IsEmpty`), borrow-returning lookups under spec §28.3's bare-type-parameter rule, the collections' existing element-slot policy, and §4.9's indexer-get posture (`GetOrNull`), renames with unchanged contracts, and doc-only convention sentences. No kernel rule added or lifted; axiom register unchanged.

**Migration.** **Newly rejected (the one BREAKING item):** the `Environment` long names — `GetEnvironmentVariable(name)` respells to `Get(name)`, `SetEnvironmentVariable(name, value)` to `Set(name, value)`, `GetEnvironmentVariables()` to `Variables()`; the long spellings become unknown-member errors. The respell is mechanical; the in-tree exposure, counted by the proposal at v0.228 and re-verified at this landing: one codegen intrinsic site (`src/codegen/LlvmBackend_Calls.cpp`, the §2.4 dispatch — 2 occurrences, comment + match) retargets its member-name string with the implementation; three conformance-corpus lines (`tests/conformance/cases/stdlib_0003.bzl`, a skip-listed signature mirror) — the corpus does **not** change at this landing and flips with the implementation, per house precedent (the v0.228 `stdlib_0101` note); proposals 0011, 0013, and 0045 (and 0072/0074's own worked examples, now pinned) keep their pinned long-name spellings and take a currency note at their next revalidation, not a retro-edit. Everything else is **additive**: seventeen `ParseOrNull` members, three `GetOrNull` members, `Console.ReadKeyOrNull`, and `String.IsEmpty` — no existing member changes shape or contract, `IParsable<T>` (§2.19) is untouched, and no grammar production, anchor, or section number moves. Newly **defined**: the `Guid.NewGuid` version-4 pin — previously implementation-chosen; a runtime whose generator is not version-4 becomes non-conforming at this revision (the shipped runtime already stamps RFC 4122 v4 bits). Doc-only: the §1 tier sentence, the §1 `Count`-vs-`Length` sentence, the §4.8 disambiguating clause, and the §4.8/§4.17 caveat prose. The conformance corpus carries no flips at this landing (verified by grep: the three `stdlib_0003.bzl` lines are the corpus's only exposure to any renamed or added name). Spec-ahead-of-impl deltas are tracked by the issues filed at this landing: [#2347](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2347) (the `ParseOrNull` intrinsics; `GetOrNull` on the three dictionaries; `ReadKeyOrNull`) and [#2348](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2348) (the `Environment` rename retarget with its corpus flip; `String.IsEmpty`; the `NewGuid` v4 conformance regression test). Proposals 0072 and 0074 flip to superseded and the README queue rows move with them. The spec and rationale texts are unchanged this revision — their companion headers move in lockstep — and the guides are untouched (their revalidation pins stand; the config-parse and lookup-with-fallback idioms join the guides at their next revalidation pass, per 0072's own migration note).

### v0.232 changelog (v0.231 → v0.232)

**Design change — the one-shot serialization facades (proposal 0073 graduates; owner-accepted 2026-07-29).** `Json` and `Binary` land as static facades in `System.Serialization` (stdlib §2.15), over the §2.15 agent pairs: whole value in, encoded form out, and back — one line at the call site, the agents invisible. Each facade member is defined normatively as the corresponding agent sequence — same options, same fault surface, byte-identical output — so the agents remain the sole semantics and the extension point (streaming, incremental writing, multi-value streams, custom formats): the §7.3 `File`-over-`FileStream` facade shape. No §2.14 vocabulary change, no agent-surface change, no new fault or payload types. The proposal's open questions Q1–Q5 are resolved at this landing:

- **The surface (stdlib §2.15; twenty-three members).** `Json`: `ToText`/`ToBytes` (each with a `JsonOptions` twin — the write family), and `Parse<T>`/`ParseOwned<T>` over six input forms each (`string` / `ReadOnlySpan<byte>` / `ReadOnlyArraySpan<byte>`, each with an options twin) — the §2.15 `JsonDeserializer` constructor set mirrored one-for-one. `Binary`: `ToBytes` plus `Parse<T>`/`ParseOwned<T>` over the `BinaryDeserializer` constructor set (`ignoreUnknownFields` on the `ReadOnlySpan<byte>` form only). **Q3 resolved as mirrored, not completed:** §2.15 declares no `(ReadOnlyArraySpan<byte>, ignoreUnknownFields)` agent constructor, so the facade declares no such form — the facade never invents surface the agent set lacks; completing both sides stays the open piggyback pin, landable by its own ruling — tracked as [#2352](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2352) now that the proposal is superseded. `Binary` has no text form — the format is bytes, and a text encoding would be an invention (composition with an encoding layer is proposal 0009's material when it lands).
- **The write family is ordinary generic code; the read family is compiler-known — stated plainly.** `ISerializable` carries a real instance method, so `ToText`/`ToBytes` are user-writable constrained generics. `IDeserializable` is a memberless marker (§2.14), so no generic body can reach the recognized `T.Deserialize(d)` factory through a constraint: `Parse<T>`/`ParseOwned<T>` (both formats) are **compiler-known generics**, on the precedent of `Task.FromResult<T>`'s compiler-special-cased class-`T` rejection (stdlib §6.7; spec §30.10). `Parse<T>` serves value-type targets — records, enums, and value-like choices (spec §9.8) — and rejects a class-typed `T` at compile time, directing to `ParseOwned<T>`; `ParseOwned<T>` serves class targets and returns `owned T` (spec §28.8). **Q2 resolved: shared-node roots stay agent-only** — a class whose recognized factory has §2.14's third shape (`owned Shared<C>`) has no facade form, `ParseOwned<C>` over it is a compile-time error, and a `ParseShared<C>` remains the mechanical later addition recorded in the proposal if a workload names it. The dispensation is temporary in principle: when rationale §5.19's recorded promotion of the recognized factory to a static interface member lands (itself gated on the `Self` return type §2.14 separately defers), all four become expressible as ordinary constrained generics with no signature change.
- **Naming (Q1, the load-bearing ruling): option (a) — the facade is named `Json`, and proposal 0019's decline register takes its amendment at this landing.** 0019 (draft) declined a `Json` static class — correctly *for its question*: a whole type for one method, when `JsonValue` is the natural home and `TryParse`/`ToJsonString` would fork across two types. Neither premise transfers to a multi-method, two-direction, typed facade whose "value type" is every `ISerializable`/`IDeserializable` conformer in the program. The amendment note in 0019's declined-alternatives register records the scoping — the decline governs the DOM's own parse entry, which stays `JsonValue.Parse` unmoved when 0019 lands; the two homes live in different modules under distinct names (`Json` the `System.Serialization` static class, `JsonValue` the future `System.Text.Json` type). The amendment rides this landing rather than 0019's graduation by owner direction — a register amendment to a draft, not a retro-edit of pinned history. **Declined with the ruling** (carried from the proposal's register): format-in-method-name naming on one `Serialization` class (a grab-bag that stutters against its own module and loses binary's per-format doorstep) and statics-on-the-agents (re-splits the facade across the write/read seam it exists to hide).
- **Faults classify under the §1 failure-signal rule (the v0.229 obligation for new fault-declaring surface).** Every facade fault condition is the defining agent sequence's own — malformed input, type mismatches, depth violations, trailing data, unknown fields under strict policy, the JSON write path's non-finite floats — raising `SerializationException` with its §2.15 typed surface. The read-side conditions classify in **band 4** under the rule's second clause, recorded beside the surface with the reason: band-3-shaped — expected at the decode boundary, information-bearing — but with no value-like error-payload type yet to carry them (the R3/R2 sequencing, v0.229), so the typed exception is the mechanism and the classification stays revisitable at the decode-cluster pilot; the write path's non-finite-float condition is inherited unmoved under §1's existing-spellings scoping sentence. No error-payload type is declared; the governance rule is engaged vacuously. **Q5 resolved by the R3(b) sequencing (restated from v0.229):** the throwing form is the facade's sole spelling under the no-dual rule; the `TryParse<T>`/`Result` dual at this seam stays **recorded, not landed** — it waits for the decode-cluster pilot under R2's adoption scope, riding proposal 0075's stages 1–2 at their own graduation. Nothing at this revision pre-commits that design.
- **Timing (Q4): `Binary` ships now, not sequenced behind proposal 0010.** The facade is defined by delegation, so 0010's per-type conformances and `WriteBytes` token work flow through with no facade-side change; nothing here touches the vocabulary 0010 froze. The binary format's same-version caveat (§2.15 *Binary mapping*) is restated at the facade's own doorstep.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** no ownership rules touched — the write members borrow their argument for the call (spec §28.3's unmarked-parameter classification) and mint fresh productions under stdlib §1's existing conventions (`string`; `owned OwningBuffer<byte>`); `ParseOwned<T>`'s `owned T` return re-surfaces the recognized factory's own §28.8 transfer; the input-span borrow inside a facade read is call-bounded — strictly shorter than the agent path's deserializer-lifetime borrow. No kernel rule added or lifted; axiom register unchanged.

**Migration.** Purely **additive**: two new static classes (`Json`, `Binary`) with twenty-three static members, declared in `System.Serialization` (explicit import, exactly as the agents); no existing member changes shape or contract, no new exception types, and no grammar production, anchor, or section number moves. Existing agent-driving code stays valid indefinitely — the agents are the facade's definition, not a deprecated tier — and the §2.15 `SavePoint`/`LoadPoint` examples gain facade-first restatements with the agent forms retained beneath as the definitional expansions. The only name effect is two new public names in an explicitly-imported module, resolved under the language's ordinary name-resolution rules like any stdlib addition. The conformance corpus carries no flips (verified by grep at landing: the corpus's one `import System.Serialization` case, `stdlib_0025.bzl`, names neither `Json` nor `Binary`). Spec-ahead-of-impl: the entire facade is unimplemented at HEAD — tracked by the implementation issue filed at this landing ([#2349](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2349): the ordinary write generics; the compiler-known read pair with its class-`T` and shared-node rejections; the byte-identical delegation property as the test oracle — noting that the `SerializationException` surface parity it asserts rides [#2337](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2337)). Proposal 0073 flips to superseded and the README queue row moves with it; proposal 0019 takes the Q1 amendment note in its declined-alternatives register. The spec text is unchanged this revision; the rationale takes one disambiguation touch — §18's informal `Json`/`Binary` labels for the v0.115 agent implementations respell to prose, now that those names are declared types in the same module — and the companion headers move in lockstep. The guides are untouched (no guide teaches the agent dance; their revalidation pins stand).

### v0.233 changelog (v0.232 → v0.233)

**Design change — `Result` ergonomics, stages 1 and 2 (proposal 0075 graduates; owner-ruled 2026-07-29, accepted as recommended).** The staged response to the first `Result`-dense Bezel program (proposal 0061 §3's evidence log): stage 1 lands **declared-result target-typing of choice-case constructions** in the language spec (§35.3, with position cross-references at §21.7, §22.2, §23.2, and §27.3 — no grammar change; the forms already parse, the edit is name resolution and typing), and stage 2 lands the four **value-payload combinators** on stdlib `Result<T, E>` (§2.20) as compiler-provided per-instantiation members (spec §35.2). Stage 3 lands nothing by design: ownership-polymorphic function parameters and any propagation operator stay recorded deferrals. The proposal's open questions Q1–Q7 are resolved at this landing:

- **Stage 1 — the rule (spec §35.3).** In a declared-result position — the top-level operand of `return e;` under a declared return type; the expression body of a member or accessor checked against its declared type; and a `return` operand or expression body checked against a lambda's return-type ascription — whose declared type (for an `async` body, the declared `Task<T>`'s result type; nullability stripped) is a choice declaring a case of the written name, the bare `N(args)` / `N` is that choice's case construction / payload-free case value. The declared type arrives whole from the signature; nothing is inferred from the construction's arguments (§14.5's posture untouched; partial qualification — `Result.Ok(v)` — stays an error), and the form resolves to a case construction *before* any classification or ownership rule runs, so payload binding, ownership, and the constructed value's classification are exactly the qualified form's. **Q1 (scope): all three position kinds ride** — §27.3 already treats `return` and the expression body as one declared-result category and equates the ascription with a declared method return; excluding `=>` would be a seam with no principle (accessor expression bodies under a declared property type join on the same ground: their block-form twins' `return` statements are §21.7 declared-result positions already). **Q2 (ambiguity): the case reading is authoritative** inside declared-choice-result positions, winning over any same-named local, parameter, member, or type in scope with a shadowing warning (qualify, bind, or rename remedy — a local or parameter cannot be qualified); scope-first-with-fallback was declined as action at a distance, §26.4's own recorded ground. **Q3 (branch positions): deferred, recorded liftable** — extending declared-result flow into `(if …)`/`(case …)` branch positions within a return operand is a §20 change with its own meet questions; the interim remedy is two `return` statements, or the qualified spelling. Also recorded, not taken: the `new()`-context family (typed locals, field initializers, default parameter values — principled but unevidenced) and enum constants (no restatement pain). The mechanism is the established declared-type-directed family (§17.7's `new()` shorthand, §4.2's typed-context widening, §15.4's return-position collection literals, §14.5 phase 3), not §14.5 inference — 0041 §2.4's recorded liftable engaged on its own stated condition: the spelling proved heavy in practice (nine restatements in one program, 0061 §3; §2.20's own listing carried the same shape).
- **Stage 2 — the members (stdlib §2.20; spec §35.2).** `Map<U>(f)`, `MapError<F>(f)`, `AndThen<U>(f)`, and `UnwrapOr(fallback)` — 0041 Q12's recorded value-payload interim, landed under **Q4's load-bearing ruling: Option A** — compiler-provided per-instantiation members on stdlib `Result` itself, admissible only where the receiver instantiation and the member's result instantiation (`Result<U, E>` / `Result<T, F>`) are both value-like — an inferred `U`/`F` that would make the result borrow-bearing or owning rejects exactly as a bad receiver does — enforced at the use site under §3.6 rule 2 (the diagnostic names the classification, the deciding payload, and the owning-match remedy). The graduation verified 0075 §3.2's mechanism finding: **Q12's recorded extension-block spelling is not available as recorded** — §26.2's extendable list never gained choices at v0.200, and no §14.2 constraint names the classification-neutral value-like bound (`value` excludes `string` and admits move-only values; `sendable` admits transfer-closed classes; there is no negated or union form; concrete-head multi-blocks collapse at the method level under §26.5.1) — so the Q12 record is amended by this ruling. **Declined: Option B** (a new classification-neutral §14.2 constraint plus a §26.2 choice admission — reusable and user-facing, but permanent constraint vocabulary bought on one program's evidence; recorded as the liftable follow-on if user-defined choices start wanting combinators) **and Option C** (the concrete-head multi-block workaround — structurally collapsed, above). §26.2's cannot-extend list now names choices explicitly. **Q5: `MapError` stays** (family symmetry). **Q6: `UnwrapOr(fallback)` confirmed** — name and parameter name (`default` is unconditionally reserved, Appendix B.1; the parameter name is API surface under §22.5's named arguments); `UnwrapOr` is total, so §2.20's no-`Unwrap` record stands undisturbed, its sentence re-worded only to say so. **Q7: function-typed payloads ride** (classification-neutral, hence value-like — harmless total value plumbing); `Result<Object, E>` is owning (§35.4 rule 1 — the `owned` marker keeps its transfer meaning at class `Object`) and is rejected like any other class-payload instantiation. None of the four is `pure` (§22.15 prohibits invoking function-typed values for the first three; `UnwrapOr` would be pure-eligible and stays plain `method` as a uniformity choice, recorded liftable); `f` is plain, hence call-bounded (§28.14); no disposal obligation arises in any combinator call, and the combinators declare no fault condition (all four total — the stdlib §1 failure-signal rule is engaged vacuously). **The value/owning asymmetry is the recorded cost of stage 2**: owning instantiations carry none of these members — a consuming `Map` needs §35.2's `this`-as-borrow lifted and §14.4's retired-and-deferred ownership-polymorphic function parameters, 0075's stage 3(a) — and the owning idiom remains the owning match, with the boundary stated in the stdlib listing so no reader first meets it at a rejected call site. Also declined, recorded: `UnwrapOrElse(f: () -> T)` (no observed need).
- **Sequencing (v0.229's R2/R5, now in their armed form).** These stages are what the R2 decode-cluster pilot rides on: `Result` adoption stays confined to the decode/deserialize and gathered-value-error clusters, enacted by per-surface graduations under R4's governance, nothing wholesale. R5's propagation-operator gate is now armed in its real form — the operator is revisited only on **observed per-call ceremony in `Result` code written with stages 1–2 available**; predicted ceremony is inadmissible, and the evidence log stays in 0061 §3. The R3(b) `TryParse<T>`/`Result` dual at proposal 0073's facade seam (v0.232 entry) continues to wait on that pilot.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** no ownership rules touched. Stage 1 is resolution and typing only — the bare form resolves to a case construction before classification runs, and from that point every existing rule applies to it *as* the qualified construction: an `owned` payload slot is the K3.3 owned-argument position, the K5 consume-site freeze applies, §35.4 classifies the constructed value, and an owning construction in return position is §28.3's ordinary announced transfer (`return Ok(owned conn);` under a declared owning instantiation means exactly what the qualified spelling means today). Stage 2 is borrow-path value plumbing at value-like instantiations: a borrowing receiver, copied or shared payload bindings, fresh copyable results, call-bounded `f`. No producers-table row, no K-clause, no Appendix C invariant changes; axiom register unchanged.

**Migration.** **Purely additive; nothing currently legal is rejected.** Newly **accepted**: the bare case forms in declared-result positions (previously ordinary-resolution errors there), and the four combinator members at value-like `Result` instantiations. Newly **warned** — the one behavioral edge: inside a declared-choice-result position, a name that both names a case of the declared type and resolves ordinarily now takes the case reading, with the shadowing warning; this re-means only a program that reads a local, parameter, or member named identically to a case of its own declared choice result type, of which the repository, the docs' examples, and the conformance corpus have none (verified by grep at landing). Newly **rejected** — one corner of the same edge: under the authoritative case reading, a call to a same-named scope member whose argument list is not a valid construction of that case is now rejected rather than resolved to the member (the warning's qualify-or-bind remedy applies); no in-tree code has such a call. Beyond that corner, nothing — a combinator call at a borrow-bearing or owning instantiation (or one whose inferred `U`/`F` would produce one) was an unknown-member error before this revision and remains an error, now with §3.6 rule 2's classification-naming diagnostic. No grammar production, anchor, or section number moves; Appendix A is untouched. The conformance corpus carries no flips. Doc-only riders: §35.3's qualified-required sentence takes the declared-result carve; §26.2's cannot-extend list names choices; stdlib §2.20's `ParsePort` and `Connect` listings respell to the stage-1 form (the qualified spellings remain valid everywhere and normative); rationale §18's sum-types entry takes the same-revision shipped annotation (the v0.201 rule), and the rationale gains §9.11 recording the declared-type-directed framing, the authoritative-vs-scope-first decision, and the recorded liftables. Spec-ahead-of-impl: both stages are unimplemented at HEAD — tracked by the two implementation issues filed at this landing ([#2354](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2354): stage-1 declared-result resolution across all three position kinds, the nullable wrapping, the async result-type rule, the shadowing warning, and the other-position did-you-mean note; [#2355](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2355): the four compiler-provided `Result` members with value-like admission, §3.6 rule 2 rejections at borrow-bearing/owning instantiations, and call-site `U`/`F` inference) — each with spec-cited regression tests per `tests/README.md`. Proposal 0075 flips to superseded (stages 1–2 graduated; its §4 stays the stage-3 deferral register) and the README queue row moves with it; 0041's Q12 record is amended by Q4's ruling as noted above; 0061 §3 remains the propagation evidence log. The guides are untouched (their revalidation pins stand; the stage-1 spelling and the combinator pipelines join Guide 2 at its next revalidation pass, per 0075 §5 — Guide 2 §6's failure-signal table is unchanged by every stage).

### v0.234 changelog (v0.233 → v0.234)

**Rulings — two critique-surfaced seams closed, one recorded contradiction fixed (owner-directed 2026-07-30).** The v0.230 and v0.232 adversarial critiques each left one item that needed a ruling rather than an edit ([#2346](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2346), [#2353](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2353)); both are ruled and landed here, together with the Appendix C contradiction [#2165](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2165) recorded at v0.220.

- **Pure members reject move-only value parameters (#2346, spec §22.15 — soundness of the fence).** §22.15 rejects `owned` parameters because their scope-end discharge runs user code inside the pure frame — but §15.3 makes the plain spelling *identical* to the `owned` spelling for a move-only value type, so `pure method P(r: Res)` over an owning choice was admitted by the letter while being spec-identical to the rejected form: the argument arrives as a value-move carrying a real owned payload whose auto-dispose runs a user destructor inside the pure call. One sentence closes the route — a move-only value parameter (owning-choice instantiation, owning inline array) is rejected like the `owned` spelling it equals, re-checked after substitution for generic parameter types (§35.11) — and the surviving plain-parameter sentence respells to "**copyable** value types and records arrive as frame-local copies", the same taxonomy respell v0.230 gave §30.5. This completes the fence the v0.230 train built: the return side (v0.230), the construction route (the v0.230 follow-up), and now the parameter route. **Declined:** admitting the parameter with defined in-frame disposal (contradicts the fragment's stated fence for no known use case) and a full-consumption obligation (not spellable — the fragment prohibits every consuming position).
- **The trailing-data fault has a defined locus (#2353, stdlib §2.15 — the gap the facades made load-bearing).** §2.15 declared trailing-data conditions raise `SerializationException` but named no operation that raises them, and the agent-path expansion contains none that could: `IDeserializer` has no end-of-input assertion, and the same `T.Deserialize(d)` call serves single-value and multi-value reads, so the runtime cannot infer whole-document intent. Ruled: trailing data is the **whole-document read forms'** condition — the `Json`/`Binary` facade reads carry a **document-exhaustion assertion** (after the root value completes, remaining non-whitespace input raises `SerializationException` from the read call itself), which is now the definition of *driven over a whole document*; the agent path deliberately never faults on remaining input (the cursor rests mid-stream for a subsequent read — exactly the multi-value idiom) and deserializer disposal never raises. This corrects the v0.232 entry's characterization of trailing data as "the defining agent sequence's own" fault — it is the facade's one addition to the delegated surface, and [#2349](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2349)'s byte-identical-delegation test oracle takes the delta (delegation plus exhaustion assertion). **Declined:** a disposal-time check (a throwing disposal poisons the §28.2 machinery) and a new `AssertEndOfInput` vocabulary member (0010-frozen surface for a condition the whole-document forms already own).
- **Appendix C narrowing invariant matches §7.4 (#2165 — the v0.220-recorded contradiction).** The compiler-enforced-invariants line still read "only local variables are narrowed", contradicting §7.4's v0.214 readonly-field rule (its own heading: "Narrowing applies to locals — and `readonly` fields — only"). The line now reads: nullable **mutable** field or property access without copying to a local is rejected; local variables and `readonly` fields (one field off an admitted root, v0.214) are narrowed. Doc-only; the implementation follows §7.4's normative text already (the #2116 redo).

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** no ownership rules touched — #2346 is an admission-set narrowing *derived* from the existing `owned`-parameter rejection plus §15.3's plain-equals-owned identity (no new rule, a closed route); #2353 defines a fault locus on library surface; #2165 restates an invariant to match its section. Axiom register unchanged.

**Migration.** Newly **rejected**: a `pure` member declaring a move-only value parameter (#2346) — the corpus carries no such declaration (zero `choice` declarations in the conformance corpus, verified at the v0.233 landing; re-verified by grep here) and no doc example declares one; spec-ahead-of-impl rides the pure-fragment enforcement generally. Newly **defined**: the trailing-data locus (#2353) — the facade reads gain the exhaustion assertion (tracked on #2349, whose oracle note updates), the agent path is pinned as never faulting on remaining input (the only implementable reading; nothing shipped enforces trailing data today, so no behavior changes at HEAD), and disposal is pinned non-throwing. Doc-only: the Appendix C reword (#2165). No grammar production, anchor, or section number moves; the conformance corpus carries no flips; the guides are untouched and keep their pins. Issues #2346, #2353, and #2165 close at this landing. The rationale text is unchanged this revision; its companion header moves in lockstep.
